NO ENGINE OR AIRCRAFT ANOMALIES WERE NOTED DURING THE POST-ACCIDENT INSPECTION THAT WOULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THIS ENGINE FAILURE, APART FROM THE AIRMAN?S FAILURE TO VISUALLY INSPECT THE FUEL TANKS PRIOR TO DEPARTURE FROM KEGT. AFTER IMPACT THE SURVIVING MEDICAL CREWMEMBERS EXTRACTED THEMSELVES FROM THE WRECKAGE AND IMMEDIATELY MADE A CELL PHONE CALL TO REPORT THEIR SITUATION AND LOCATION. SEVERAL AGENCIES THEN USED THE POSITION REPORT FROM THE CREW, DATA FROM THE ON-BOARD GPS POSITION REPORTING SYSTEM, AND SIGNALS FROM THE 406 MHZ EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER TO LOCATE THE WRECKAGE. EMERGENCY RESPONDERS HIKED IN THE DARK NIGHT CONDITIONS THROUGH THE REMOTE RUGGED TERRAIN AND ARRIVED SEVERAL HOURS LATER. 20150313003109I	ON 3/13/2015, WHILE ON APPROACH TO LINCOLN PARK AIRPORT (NO7), A ROCKWELL COMMANDER AIRCRAFT (N7MA) HAD AN INDICATION THAT THE NOSE LANDING GEAR WAS NOT FULLY DOWN AND LOCKED. THE PILOT CYCLED THE LANDING GEAR, AT WHICH POINT HE CONFIRMED THAT THE REQUIRED THREE DOWN AND LOCKED GREEN LIGHTS WHERE ON. HE THEN, CONTACTED A HELICOPTER FLYING NEARBY AND GROUND PERSONNEL (NAMES NOT AVAILABLE) TO VERIFY THAT ALL THREE LANDING GEAR WERE DOWN. UPON RECEIVING VERBAL CONFIRMATION THE PILOT CONTINUED THE APPROACH AND LANDED THE AIRCRAFT. DURING ROLL OUT THE NOSE LANDING GEAR COLLAPSED CAUSING THE PROPELLER TO CONTACT THE RUNWAY BRINGING THE AIRCRAFT TO A FULL STOP.   DURING THE POST INCIDENT INVESTIGATION OF THE AIRCRAFT THE FOLLOWING ISSUES WERE DISCOVERED. 1)	THE AIRCRAFT WAS BEING RELOCATED FROM SUSSEX COUNTY AIRPORT (KFWN) WHERE MAINTENANCE (UNRELATED TO THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM) HAD JUST BEEN PERFORMED. THE PILOT SAID HE WAS UNAWARE THAT THE MAINTENANCE PERFORMED WAS NOT ENTERED INTO THE AIRCRAFT LOG BOOK, NOR WAS HE PROVIDED WITH A LOG BOOK ENTRY BEFORE TAKING THE AIRCRAFT AND DEPARTING FOR LINCOLN PARK.  2)	A VIDEO THAT HAD BEEN TAKEN OF THE AIRCRAFT LANDING CLEARLY SHOWED THE NOSE GEAR WAS NOT FULLY EXTENDED AND IN THE DOWN AND LOCKED POSITION. 3)	AFTER THE AIRCRAFT WAS TOWED INTO A HANGAR AND PLACED ON JACKS, THE NOSE GEAR ACTUATOR WAS DISCONNECTED ALLOWING THE NOSE GEAR TO MOVE FREELY INTO THE FULL DOWN LOCKED POSITION. 4)	POWER WAS THEN APPLIED TO THE AIRCRAFT AND WHEN THE LANDING GEAR LIGHTS WERE CHECKED, THEY INDICATED RIGHT AND LEFT MAIN GEAR DOWN AND LOCKED BUT THE NOSE INDICATED NOT DOWN AND LOCKED (NO LIGHT).THE BULB WAS CHECKED USING THE SYSTEM PRESS TO TEST AND WAS DETERMINED TO WORK NORMALLY. EVEN WITH THE ACTUATOR DISCONNECTED, THE NOSE LIGHT SHOULD HAVE BEEN ?ON?. THIS INDICATES THAT THERE MAY BE A FAULT OR MULTIPLE FAULTS IN THE INDICATION CIRCUIT PREVENTING THE LIGHT FROM COMING ON OR GIVING A FALSE GREEN INDICATION WHEN THE GEAR WAS NOT DOWN AND LOCKED. THIS COULD EXPLAIN WHY THE PILOT SAID HE HAD THREE GREEN LIGHTS WHEN THE GEAR WAS NOT DOWN AND LOCKED. 5)	INSPECTION OF THE FLUID LEVEL IN THE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM RESERVOIR  WAS CHECKED AND FOUND TO BE BELOW THE LOWEST READABLE LEVELOF THE UNIT?S DIP STICK INDICATING THERE WAS  LITTLE OR NO FLUID IN THE SYSTEM. THE LACK OF FLUID IN THE SYSTEM COULD HAVE PREVENTED THE NOSE ACTUATOR FROM FULLY EXTENDING.     6)	 DAMAGE TO THE NOSE LANDING GEAR ACTUATOR SHAFT SUGGESTS THE ACTUATOR WAS NOT FULLY EXTENDED BY APPROXIMATELY 2 INCHES.  ON 3/20/2015 THE ACTUATOR WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO THE MANUFACTURER FOR TEAR DOWN AND EVALUATION. ANY ADDITIONAL PERTINENT INFORMATION FROM THE RESULTS OF THE ACTUATOR TEAR DOWN, HYDRAULIC SYSTEM LOW FLUID LEVEL AND THE MALFUNCTIONING LANDING GEAR INDICATION CIRCUIT WILL BE ADDED IN AN AMENDMENT TO THIS REPORT.  AMENDMENT MAY 5, 2015- AFTER BEING CONTACTED BY THE ACTUATOR MANUFACTURER, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ACTUATOR WAS OPERATING NORMALLY AND THE TEAR DOWN INDICATED IT HAD ALL THE CORRECT SEALS AND O-RINGS INSTALLED.  WITH THIS NEW INFORMATION, IT IS DETERMINED THAT THE MOST PROBABLE CAUSE OF THE NOSE LANDING GEAR NOT FULLY EXTENDING WOULD BE THE LACK OF HYDRAULIC FLUID IN THE SYSTEM. THIS, CONNECTED WITH THE FAILURE OF THE PILOT TO FOLLOW THE AIRCRAFT EMERGENCY CHECKLIST AND PULL THE EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR EXTENSION HANDLE ARE THE MOST LIKELY PROBABLE  OF THIS INCIDENT..  THIS INCIDENT IS NOW CLOSED. NO FURTHER ACTION TO BE TAKEN.

THE AFT SERVICE DOOR WAS NOT NEEDED BECAUSE ALL PASSENGERS EVACUATED FROM OVERWING EXITS AND FORWARD PASSENGER ENTRY DOOR.  4. WHETHER ANY EXIT SLIDES, OR ASSOCIATE COMPONENTS MALFUNCTIONED AND, IF SO, WHAT WERE THE MALFUNCTIONS. THERE WERE NO SLIDE OR EXIT MALFUNCTIONS.  5. THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN MOVED AWAY FROM THE TERMINAL BUILDING FOR SAFETY AND FIRE PREVENTION THE PREVIOUS DAY, TO A LOCATION AT MID-RAMP.  AS A RESULT OF IMPACT WITH THE TERMINAL BUILDING AND SUPPORTING STEEL UPRIGHTS, THE CRANKSHAFT FLANGE HAD CRACKED AND THE PROPELLER HAD BECOME DETACHED. THE WINGS HAD STRUCK TWO STEEL UPRIGHTS (FIRST WITH THE RIGHT WING AND THEN THE LEFT WING) CAUSING THE LEFT WING LIFT STRUT TO BECOME DETACHED AT THE LOWER ATTACH POINT AND RESULTING IN DEEP LEADING EDGE DENTS AND SKIN PERFORATION AND TEARING BACK TO THE MAIN SPAR ON BOTH WINGS, INCLUDING LEFT WING SPAR DISTORTION. THERE WAS SIGNIFICANT WRINKLING AND DISTORTION OF THE LH SIDE FUSELAGE SKIN. WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF AN ACCOMPANYING AIRWORTHINESS INSPECTOR, WE REMOVED THE UPPER LEFT AND RIGHT ENGINE COWLING TO GAIN ACCESS TO THE ENGINE MAGNETOS.  WE FOUND THAT THE MAGNETOS WERE UNCOMPROMISED AND INTACT.  THE IGNITION WIRING AND MAGNETO PRIMARY LEADS WERE APPROPRIATELY CONNECTED AND UNCOMPROMISED FROM THE IMPACT WITH THE TERMINAL BUILDING.  I ATTEMPTED TO CONTACT THE FIRST RESPONDERS TO THE SCENE TO LEARN OF THE POSITION OF THE MAGNETO SWITCH AND ENGINE CONTROLS.  I WAS ADVISED BY THE AIRPORT MANAGER THAT HE WAS NOT THE FIRST PERSON TO ENTER THE AIRCRAFT, BUT WAS THE PERSON CALLED TO SECURE THE AIRCRAFT.  FIRST RESPONDERS HAD REMOVED THE UNINJURED FEMALE PASSENGER FROM THE RIGHT FRONT SEAT AS THE ENGINE CONTINUED TO RUN AT FULL POWER DESPITE THE CRANKSHAFT BEING SHEARED AT THE PROPELLER FLANGE.  THE AIRPORT MANAGER STATED THAT THE MAGNETO SWITCH WAS IN THE ?L? (LEFT) POSITION, AND THAT THE ENGINE THROTTLE WAS FULL FORWARD (FULL THROTTLE) AND THAT THE MIXTURE CONTROL WAS AT FULL RICH. WITH THE ENGINE CONTROLS IN THIS POSITION, THE MAGNETO WOULD HAVE BEEN ABLE TO PRODUCE CURRENT TO THE ENGINE SPARK PLUGS AND IGNITE ANY FUEL REMAINING IN THE CYLINDERS.  ON TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS VIA CELL PHONE VOICE MAIL, I ASKED THE PILOT^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ TO PROVIDE ME WITH AIRCRAFT AND ENGINE LOG BOOKS TO VERIFY ANNUAL INSPECTION DATES.  NO RETURN PHONE CALL WAS RECEIVED FROM ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^PILOT.  NO LOG BOOK ENTRIES WERE RECEIVED FROM HIM.-END WDG

THE JUMP HE WAS PARTICIPATING IN WAS HIS 7TH JUMP OF THE DAY. THE EQUIPMENT HE WAS WEARING WAS HIS OWN EQUIPMENT WHICH HE HAD BEEN JUMPING FOR MANY YEARS. HE WAS OBSERVED BY HIS WIFE PACKING HIS MAIN CANOPY PRIOR TO THE LAST JUMP.  INVESTIGATION OF THE JUMPER?S EQUIPMENT WAS CONDUCTED. THE EQUIPMENT INVOLVED IS IDENTIFIED AS FOLLOWS:  HARNESS & CONTAINER: MIRAGE SYSTEMS  MT, BUILT 3/2001 MAIN CANOPY:  CROSSFIRE 109  (109 SQ FT CANOPY)  RESERVE CANOPY: PERFORMANCE DESIGN PR-126 BUILT 11/2000. RESERVE PACKING CARD INDICATES RESERVE LAST PACKED FEB. 26, 2015. AAD EQUIPMENT: CYPRESS ORIGINALLY INSTALLED IN EQUIPMENT WAS NO LONGER INSTALLED.  FINDINGS DURING THE EQUIPMENT INSPECTION CONCLUDED THE FOLLOWING:  	 1.	THE CUT-AWAY HANDLE BEING LOCATED AWAY FROM THE BODY ALONG THE PREVIOUS FLIGHT PATH INDICATES A CONSCIOUS EFFORT TO MAKE A "CUT AWAY" OF THE MAIN PARACHUTE FROM THE HARNESS. THIS COULD INDICATE THE JUMPER WAS AWARE THAT HE HAD SOME TYPE OF MALFUNCTION. 2.	THE MAIN PARACHUTE CONTAINER CLOSING LOOP HAD BEEN CUT/SHEARED OFF JUST BELOW THE AREA WHERE THE PIN WOULD HAVE ENGAGED IN THE LOOP AND ABOVE THE CONTAINER GROMMETS. THE CLOSING PIN WAS SLIGHTLY BENT AND HAD MARKS WHICH CORRESPOND TO EXCESSIVE FORCE BEING APPLIED AGAINST THE CONTAINER CLOSING FLAP GROMMETS. THE TOP CLOSING FLAP GROMMET WAS DEFORMED AS WELL TO MATCH THE IMPRINT OF THE CLOSING PIN. THESE FINDINGS ARE INDICATORS THAT THE PIN HOLDING THE MAIN PARACHUTE IN THE HARNESS/CONTAINER WAS STILL ENGAGED (HOLDING THE CONTAINER CLOSED) AT THE TIME OF IMPACT. 3.	THE MAIN PARACHUTE PILOT CHUTE HAD INDICATIONS THAT IT MAY HAVE BEEN IN A PARTIALLY COCKED CONDITION. THIS WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE PILOT CHUTE TO NOT PRODUCE OPTIMUM DRAG IF IT HAD BEEN IN THE AIRSTREAM. THERE WAS NO CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE THE PILOT CHUTE HAD BEEN DEPLOYED, BUT IF IT HAD BEEN IT EITHER DID NOT HAVE SUFFICIENT TIME TO INFLATE TO PULL THE MAIN CONTAINER CLOSING PIN, OR WAS NOT EFFECTIVE IN PULLING THE MAIN CONTAINER CLOSING PIN.  4.	THE RESERVE RIPCORD HANDLE HAD NOT BEEN ACTIVATED, AND THE RESERVE PIN & SEAL WERE STILL IN PLACE. THIS INDICATES THE JUMPER DID NOT INITIATE DEPLOYMENT OF HIS RESERVE PARACHUTE. 5.	THE HARNESS/CONTAINER ORIGINALLY HAD AN AAD INSTALLED.  SOMETIME AFTER 2013 THIS EQUIPMENT WAS REMOVED, ACCORDING TO THE JUMPERS WIFE BECAUSE IT HAD ?TURNED INTO A PUMPKIN? (EXCEEDED ITS LIFE LIMIT). NO AUTOMATIC OPENING DEVICE WAS INSTALLED IN THE EQUIPMENT AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. 6.	THE EQUIPMENT WAS IN SERVICE

20150531013389A	ACCIDENT OCCURRED ON MAY 31ST, 2015 AT APPROXIMATELY 8PM.  THE STUDENT PILOT/PIC HAD PLANNED A GOOSE BAY, TALKEETNA, AND SKWENTNA,  ALASKA SOLO CROSS-COUNTRY FLIGHT. PIC SAID THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED AS HE WAS "DRAGGING THE RUNWAY" AT A FRIENDS CABIN THAT IS LOCATED AT 61.791489N, 150.93634W OR ABOUT 3 NM NNW OF ALEXANDER LAKE, ALASKA.  ALEXANDER LAKE IS APPROXIMATELY 15NM SE OF THE SKWENTNA AIRPORT.    THE PIC STATED HE HAD INTENDED TO LAND AT TALKEETNA BUT THERE HAD BEEN AN ACCIDENT THERE AND HE DIVERTED BECAUSE OF THIS.  PIC STATED HIS INTENT WAS TO DRAG THE RUNWAY AT HIS FRIENDS CABIN BECAUSE HE "WASN'T LEGAL TO LAND THERE" BY HIS CFI.    HE HAD PLANNED A LOW APPROACH TO THE NORTH WITH A SLIGHT QUARTERING CROSSWIND (HE EST. APPROX 5 KNOTS).  AS HE APPROACHED THE RUNWAY, COMING IN OVER THE TREES AND DESCENDING THROUGH AN ESTIMATED 200' HE HAD "1 NOTCH" OF FLAPS EXTENDED, THE MIXTURE WAS SLIGHTLY LEANED WITH CARBURETOR HEAT ON/HOT.    THE PIC STATED THE AIRCRAFT "SUNK HARD"--HE ADDED POWER--PERHAPS TOO FAST BY HIS OWN ADMISSION, AND HE BELIEVES THIS IS WHAT CAUSED THE ENGINE TO LOSE POWER.          THE PIC IS ALSO A CERTIFICATED MECHANIC AND HAD DONE MUCH OF THE MAINTENANCE ON THE AIRCRAFT.  THERE'S AN AIRWORTHINESS DIRECTIVE FOR THIS AIRCRAFT/ENGINE EQUIPPED WITH SCHEBLER CARBURETOR MODEL MA-4-SPA (#73-09-06) "TO PREVENT POWER INTERRUPTION AND ACCELERATION HANGUP RESULTING FROM ABRUPT THROTTLE MOVEMENT".  THERE'S A REQUIRED PLACARD THAT STATES "DO NOT OPEN THROTTLE RAPIDLY -- (IDLE TO FULL THROTTLE, 2 SECONDS MINIMUM".    THE PIC'S THEORY FOR THE MISHAP WAS THAT HE WAITED TOO LONG TO APPLY POWER AND THEN APPLIED POWER TOO FAST AND THIS IS WHAT HAD CAUSED THE ENGINE TO LOSE POWER AND HIM TO EVENTUALLY IMPACT THE GROUND.    PIC STATED THAT WITH THE THROTTLE FULL IN THE ENGINE WILL DIE AND THE ONLY WAY TO GET THE ENGINE BACK IS TO BACK THE THROTTLE OFF TO APPROXIMATELY 50% AND WAIT.  THE PIC ALSO STATED THAT THIS HAD OCCURRED BEFORE BUT NEVER THIS LOW TO THE GROUND.    THE PIC STATED THE AIRCRAFT CAME DOWN HARD, LEFT TRACKS FOR ABOUT 25', BOUNCED BACK INTO THE AIR AND OVER A DIRT PILE.  THE LEFT WING HIT A BIRCH TREE AND CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO SPIN AROUND 180 DEG. BEFORE IT CAME TO A STOP WHICH THE PIC THOUGHT SERIOUSLY SIDE LOADED THE LANDING GEAR.  THE PIC STATED HE WAS NOT INJURED EXCEPT FOR A SORE BACK.  AFTER HE CAME TO A STOP HE SHUT POWER OFF, AND THEN SHUT THE ELT OFF TO AVOID AN UNNECESSARY RESCUE COORDINATION CENTER RESPONSE.

20150601011989A	A BELL 206, N73AW, REPORTED ENGINE PROBLEMS, WHICH CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO AUTOROTATE IN A FIELD NEAR DEWEY, AZ., ON 6/2/15.  THE HELICOPTER WAS OWNED AND OPERATED BY AIR MEDICAL SERVICES OF GLENDALE, AZ. AND WAS BEING FERRIED FROM VALLE AIRPORT, GRAND CANYON AZ. (40G) TO GLENDALE MUNICIPAL AIRPORT, AZ (GEU), WHEN THE INCIDENT OCCURRED.  DAMAGE TO THE HELICOPTER WAS SUBSTANTIAL.  THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE LONE OCCUPANT OF THE HELICOPTER, THE PILOT.  IT WAS DETERMINED AT THE TIME THAT WEATHER WAS NOT A FACTOR.     THE PILOTS STATED THAT WHILE HE WAS ENROUTE HE HEARD AN AUDIBLY LOUD POP CORRESPONDING WITH A RED ENGINE OUT LIGHT AND ENGINE OUT HORN.  THE PILOT IMMEDIATELY LOCATED A SAFE AREA TO LAND AND ENTERED INTO AN AUTOROTATION.  DURING THE DESCENT HE WAS ABLE TO CONFIRM THAT THE ENGINE WAS OUT.  HE ATTEMPTED TO ROLLED THROTTLE TO THE DETENT/IDLE POSITION, BUT NO CHANGE OCCURRED. AFTER LANDING HE NOTED THAT THE MAIN ROTOR AND TAIL ROTOR BLADES WERE FREEWHEELING UNTIL THEY SLOWED TO A STOP.  AFTER EXITING THE AIRCRAFT, HE SAW NOTICEABLE DAMAGE TO VARIOUS PARTS OF TAIL SECTION.  HE STATED THAT PRIOR TO THE ENGINE OUT, WHILE ENROUTE, THERE WERE TWO SEPARATE OCCURRENCES WHERE THE ENGINE CHIP LIGHT FLASHED ON AND OFF MOMENTARILY.    PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT THE AIRCRAFT HAD HAD TWO OTHER ENGINE CHIP LIGHTS RECORDED IN THE LOGBOOKS.  ON THE FIRST OCCASION, MAINTENANCE DID NOT FIND ANY METAL PARTICLES OR SLUDGE ON THE CHIP DETECTORS OR IN THE FILTER.  THE FILTER WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED AND THE ENGINE WAS RAN AND CHECK GOOD.  ON THE SECOND OCCASION, MAINTENANCE DID NOT FIND ANY EVIDENCE OF METAL PARTICLES AGAIN.  THE OPERATOR DECIDED TO HAVE THE OIL ANALYZED BY A LABORATORY.  THE AIRCRAFT REMAINED AT VALLE AIRPORT UNTIL THE OIL ANALYSIS WAS RETURNED.  OIL ANALYSIS WAS SENT TO AOA TRIBOLOGY AND CAME BACK ?ALL VALUES APPEAR NORMAL?.  THIS WAS VERIFIED VIA DOCUMENTATION. AFTER THE LABORATORY RESULTS CAME BACK NORMAL, THE OPERATOR DECIDED TO FERRY THE AIRCRAFT BACK TO THE MAINTENANCE BASE FOR FURTHER TROUBLESHOOTING.  AFTER THE AIRCRAFT WAS RELEASED AND TRANSPORTED TO GLENDALE MUNICIPAL AIRPORT, THE CHIP DETECTOR PLUGS WERE REMOVED.  BOTH UPPER RT AND LOWER LT (POWER), CHIP PLUGS WERE FULL OF METAL FLAKES AND SLUDGE, WELL IN EXCESS OF THE ALLOWABLE LIMITS AS NOTED IN THE  MAINTENANCE MANUAL. THERE WERE NO OTHER INDICATIONS NOTED.    THE NTSB AND THE FAA EXAMINED THE AIRCRAFT AND THE ENGINE.  ONCE THE INLET COWL WAS TAKEN OFF, THE COMPRESSOR BLADES COULD BE SEEN COATED WITH GREY RESIDUE, INDICATIVE OF THE COMPRESSOR SEIZING.   IT WAS AT THIS TIME THAT THE NTSB AND THE BELL REPRESENTATIVE DECIDED TO HAVE THE ENGINE SHIPPED AND TORN DOWN AT THE ROLLS ROYCE SERVICE CENTER IN INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA.  THE TEAR-DOWN REPORT WILL BE FORWARDED TO THE FAA IIC PENDING COMPLETION.   DAMAGE TO THE HELICOPTER INCLUDED THE FOLLOWING: MAIN ROTOR BLADE MADE CONTACT WITH THE VERTICAL FINS AND TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT WHILE FREE-SPINNING AND NOT UNDER POWER.  INSPECTIONS REQUIRED ARE; OVERHAULS OF THE MAIN ROTOR MAST, MAIN ROTOR HUB, SWASH PLATE, FREEWHEELING UNIT, MAIN ROTOR PITCH LINKS, SEVERAL CONTROL TUBES, AND ENGINE.  INSPECTION OF THE MAIN ROTOR BLADES MUST ALSO BE ACCOMPLISHED.  TAILBOOM, TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT, VERTICAL FINS AND MAIN ROTOR DRIVESHAFT HAVE TO BE REPLACED.

THE OPENED LANDING GEAR MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER  , THE BENT RETRACT RODS, DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT, AND LACK OF DAMAGE TO THE GEAR, IS ALL INDICATIVE OF THE LANDING GEAR TRYING TO LIFT THE AIRCRAFT OFF THE RUNWAY AND OVERLOADING SYSTEM. A QUICK CHECK OF THE GAUGES SHOWED THAT THE ALTERNATOR DRAW WAS NO LONGER WORKING. I MADE A 180 TURN TO HEADING OF 90 TO ENTER DOWNWIND LEG FOR LANDING AT RUNWAY 17. AT THIS POINT I TURNED THE STROBE LIGHTS OFF TO CONSERVE POWER AND CHECKED ALL CIRCUIT BREAKERS (NO BREAKERS WERE TRIPPED). AT THIS POINT I HAD CROSSED THE RUNWAY AND WAS AT PATTERN ELEVATION. I ENTERED THE DOWNWIND LEG, CHECKED FOR PROPER AIR SPEED (LESS THAN 120 MPH) AND ACTIVATED THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM. AT THIS TIME MY RADIOS WENT SILENT BUT I FELT AND HEARD THE CLICK AS THE LANDING GEAR DOORS OPENED AND FELT THE BUMP THAT THE GEAR NORMALLY MAKES WHEN GOING INTO LANDING CONFIGURATION, ALTHOUGH DUE TO LACK OF ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS NO AFFIRMATIVE LANDING GEAR LIGHTS WERE ILLUMINATED. AS I NEARED THE END OF THE RUNWAY I APPLIED 10 DEGREE FLAPS AND CONTINUED MY APPROACH TO THE RUNWAY. I TURNED TO BASE LEG AND APPLIED 25 DEGREES OF FLAPS WHILE SLOWING TO 85 MPH LANDING SPEED. AS I TURNED TO FINAL AND APPLIED FULL FLAPS, I NOTED A BI-PLANE HAD NOT YET CLEARED THE ACTIVE RUNWAY. I APPLIED FULL THROTTLE AND CIRCLED BACK TO THE DOWNWIND LEG FOR A SECOND ATTEMPT AT THE LANDING. AS I ENTERED THE FINAL APPROACH WITH FLAPS FULLY EXTENDED AND GLIDE SPEED OF 85 MPH, I PRAYED LORD LET THE GEAR BE DOWN. AS I CAME DOWN THE RUNWAY ON GLIDE PATH, I BEGAN TO FLARE A COUPLE OF FEET ABOVE THE RUNWAY. THE PLANE BEGAN TO SETTLE DOWN AND I PULLED BACK ON THE THROTTLE. THE PROP HIT THEN THE PLANE BEGAN TO SKID STRAIGHT DOWN THE RUNWAY COMING TO A STOP ABOUT 800 FEET FROM TOUCHDOWN POINT. WHILE SLIDING I HAD TURNED THE IGNITION OFF AND REMOVED THE KEY AS WELL AS PULLED THE MIXTURE TO FULL LEAN. ONCE THE PLANE CAME TO A STOP, I QUICKLY REMOVED ALL SEAT BELTS AND EXITED THE PLANE. AFTER LEAVING THE PLANE I PROCEEDED TO THE FBO TO MAKE SURE THE PROPER AUTHORITIES WERE NOTIFIED OF THE INCIDENT. 20150701012229I	SUMMARY: FLIGHT CREW WAS UNABLE TO DETERMINE CROSSWIND OR TAILWIND COMPONENT BUT FAILED TO EXECUTE A GO AROUND BELIEVING THEY WERE NOT EXCEEDING LIMITS OR CAPABILITIES OF THE AIRCRAFT.  THE INVESTIGATION OF THIS INCIDENT HAS REVEALED THE FOLLOWING. THE FLIGHT LANDED ON RUNWAY 16R IN DENVER DURING RAPIDLY CHANGING WIND CONDITIONS. THIS RESULTED IN A TAIL WIND DURING THE LANDING THAT EXCEEDED COMPANY AIRCRAFT LIMITATIONS. A HOT BRAKE SITUATION OCCURRED AFTER THE LANDING PRIMARILY DUE TO THE AMOUNT OF DIFFERENTIAL BRAKING REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN AIRCRAFT CONTROL DURING THE LANDING ROLLOUT. DURING THE AIRCRAFT APPROACH TO LANDING THE TOWER CONTROLLER WAS SURPRISED BY THE WIND SWITCH AND SUBSEQUENTLY REPORTED THE WINDS TO THE FLIGHT CREW ON FINAL APPROACH APPROXIMATELY ONE MINUTE 50 SECONDS BEFORE LANDING. THE CREW INCORRECTLY INTERPRETED THESE TOWER REPORTED WINDS AS CROSSWINDS.  THE FLIGHT CREW, THINKING THEY WERE LANDING WITH A CROSSWIND ONLY, CONTINUED THE APPROACH AND SUBSEQUENT LANDING. THEY DID NOT UNDERSTAND THE CROSSWIND OR TAILWIND COMPONENTS WHICH MAY HAVE EXCEEDED THE COMPANY LIMITATIONS FOR THE AIRCRAFT. IN THE MOMENTS LEADING UP TO THE ACCIDENT, THE HELICOPTER WAS SLOWED DOWN AND A LEFT TURN WAS INITIATED. THE REDUCTION IN AIRSPEED AND TURN DOWNWIND FROM THE PREVAILING WINDS RESULTED IN A REDUCTION IN TRANSLATIONAL LIFT, EFFECTIVELY REQUIRING A HIGHER ANGLE OF ATTACK FROM THE MAIN ROTOR BLADES TO MAINTAIN THE HOVER, WHICH RESULTED IN AN INCREASE IN POWER REQUIRED FROM THE ENGINE. ADDITIONALLY, A LEFT TURN IN THIS TYPE OF HELICOPTER REQUIRES AN INCREASE IN ANGLE OF ATTACK AND MORE THRUST PRODUCTION FROM THE TAIL ROTOR, ALSO RESULTING IN MORE POWER REQUIRED FROM THE ENGINE. THE LACK OF AVAILABLE POWER LED TO THE LOW ROTOR RPM AND SUBSEQUENT LOSS OF LIFT.

AT AROUND 25KIAS SIC REPORTED THAT HE ?WASN?T SURE THE ENGINE HAD FULLY QUIT (SPEAKING OF #2 ENGINE WHICH WAS PRESUMED TO BE THE BAD ENGINE?) AND THAT THEY NEEDED TO LOSE SOME MORE WEIGHT.  THE PIC, USING THE CYCLIC EMERGENCY HOOK RELEASE BUTTON, ATTEMPTED TO JETTISON THE BUCKET AND RIGGING, BUT THEY DID NOT DROP CLEAR FROM THE AIRCRAFT.  THE PIC ORDERED SIC TO ?USE THE EMERGENCY THROTTLE? AND SIC  DID THIS AND REPORTED THAT ?THE ENGINE IS NOT RESPONDING? (SIC REPORTS THAT HE ACTIVATED BOTH EMERGENCY THROTTLES OR MANUAL THROTTLES, HOWEVER AT THE ACCIDENT SITE ONLY THE #2 ENGINE MANUAL THROTTLE LEVER WAS ACTIVATED (COPILOTS STORY HAS SOME INCONSISTENCIES IN THIS REGARD)).  AT THIS POINT, WITH ROTOR SPEED CONTINUING TO DECAY (COPILOT REPORTED #1 ENGINE WAS INDICATING 722 T5 AND WAS PRESUMED TO BE THE GOOD ENGINE), THE PIC FOUND A PLACE TO MAKE AN EMERGENCY LANDING.  IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE GROUND WHILE MANEUVERING TO LAND, THE BUCKED BECAME ENTANGLED IN A BARBED WIRE FENCE AND AROUND A TREE.  THE LONG LINE PULLED TIGHT AND THE AIRCRAFT IMPACTED GROUND ON ITS TAIL WHEEL FOLLOWED MOMENTARILY BY THE LEFT MAIN GEAR THEN RIGHT MAIN GEAR.  THE TAIL WHEEL STRUT FAILED AND SEPARATED FROM THE AIRCRAFT.  WITH THE TAIL WHEEL MISSING (GROUND SCARS SHOW) THE TAIL ROTOR BRIEFLY CONTACTED THE GROUND AND APPEARS TO HAVE SEPARATED THE TAIL ROTOR DRIVE SHAFT AT THE TAIL ROTOR GEAR BOX INPUT COUPLING.  IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE TIME OF AIRCRAFT GROUND IMPACT, THE LONG LINE PHYSICALLY SEPARATED FROM THE AIRCRAFT. THE COMBINATION TO HIGH MAIN ROTOR PITCH SETTING (FOR LANDING IN ROTOR DROOP CONDITION), LOSS OF TAIL ROTOR ANTI-TORQUE FUNCTION (FORM GROUND IMPACT), AND THE AIRCRAFT BECOMING UNRESTRICTED BY LONG LINE SEPARATION, CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO TIP FORWARD AND THE MAIN ROTOR BLADES TO CONTACT THE GROUND.  ONCE MAIN ROTORS CONTACTED THE GROUND, THE RIGHT MAIN GEAR COLLAPSED AND SEPARATED, THE TAIL PIVOTED TO THE RIGHT AND THE AIRCRAFT ROLLED ON ITS SIDE CAUSING SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE. ACCIDENT SITE DEBRIS AND GROUND SCARS DEMONSTRATE THAT THE ENTANGLED BUCKET AND LINE CONTRIBUTED SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE AIRCRAFT LANDING IN AN UNINTENDED POSITION AND ATTITUDE, AND APPEARS TO HAVE CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO ROLL ON ITS SIDE AFTER LANDING.

DURING A TELEPHONE CONVERSATION, THE MECHANIC THAT REPLACED THE CYLINDERS STATED THAT HE HAD PROPERLY TORQUED THE NUTS, USED A CALIBRATED TORQUE WRENCH AND THE MOST CURRENT MANUFACTURER?S TECHNICAL DATA TO PERFORM THE TASK. HE ALSO SAID THAT THE COMPANY WHERE HE PERFORMED THE WORK WAS OUT OF BUSINESS AND ALL RECORDS, TECHNICAL DATA AND TOOLING WERE DISCARDED. THE TORQUE WRENCH HE USED IS NO LONGER AVAILABLE FOR INSPECTION BY THE FAA. AS THERE WAS NO WAY TO PROVE CONCLUSIVELY THAT THIS MECHANIC IMPROPERLY TORQUED THE NUTS, A COMPLIANCE ACTION CONSISTING OF COUNSELING HAS BEEN COMPLETED WITH THE MECHANIC AND DOCUMENTED ACCORDINGLY.  THE ENGINE WAS LAST OVERHAULED FEBRUARY 8, 2000 AT A TIME SINCE NEW OF 2616.8 HOURS. AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, IT HAD ACCUMULATED 1114.0 HOURS SINCE MAJOR OVERHAUL. THE ENGINE MANUFACTURER RECOMMENDS 2000 HOURS OR 12 YEARS BETWEEN OVERHAULS.  IF ANY ADDITIONAL INFORMATION BECOMES AVAILABLE THIS REPORT WILL BE AMENDED AS NECESSARY.

THE PARACHUTIST LANDED ON THE GROUND BETWEEN TWO TENTS. THIS WAS A DELIBERATE ACTION TO AVOID LANDING ON A LARGE NUMBER OF SEATED SPECTATORS THAT WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO GET OUT OF HIS WAY.  HIS ACTION MAY VERY WELL HAVE PREVENTED SEVERE INJURIES TO SEVERAL PEOPLE.

20151031022459I	I WAS ASSIGNED THE INCIDENT ON 11/02/2015.  THIS OFFICE WAS FIRST MADE AWARE OF THE INCIDENT BY THE OWNER/OPERATOR CONTACTING THE FSDO.  I CONTACTED THE ROC AND LET THEM KNOW AND THEY INSTRUCTED ME TO SEND AN 8020-9 WHEN POSSIBLE.  I THEN CONTACTED THE OPERATOR AND HE GAVE A VERBAL ACCOUNT OF WHAT OCCURRED.  HE STATED THAT THE LOCKING HANDLE WAS NOT FULLY ENGAGED WHEN THE DOOR BLEW OFF.  ON 11/03/2015, I TRAVELED TO PINE MOUNTAIN/HARRIS COUNTY AIRPORT (KPIM).  I INSPECTED THE AIRCRAFT AND TALKED WITH THE LOCAL FIELD A&P MECHANIC WHO WITNESSED THE AIRCRAFT LAND AND ASSISTED WITH SERVICING THE AIRCRAFT.  N700TC IS A 1980 PIPER AEROSTAR 601P SERIAL NUMBER 61P07718063384. THE INCIDENT FLIGHT WAS FOR LEISURE (PART 91) WITH PASSENGER (SPOUSE) ABOARD.  THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED MINIMAL DAMAGE WHEN THE AIRCRAFT ENTRY DOOR (UPPER CLAMSHELL DOOR) SEPARATED IN FLIGHT.  UPON INSPECTION, ONLY MINOR SCRATCHES ON THE EXTERIOR PAINT OF THE FUSELAGE, JUST AFT OF THE DOOR FRAME WERE DISCOVERED. I BELIEVE THAT DAMAGE WAS MINIMIZED DUE TO THE RAPID DEPRESSURIZATION FORCE AND THE CLIMBING PITCH ANGLE CAUSING THE DOOR TO RIP FROM ITS PIANO HINGE AND CLEAR THE AIRCRAFT WITHOUT MAKING FURTHER CONTACT.    THE OWNER STATED THAT PROFESSIONAL AVIAITION MANAGEMENT FROM MILLERSBURG, OH WAS GOING TO DO AN EDDY CURRENT INSPECTION ON THE DOOR FRAME STRUCTURE, BUT DID NOT GIVE ME A DATE.  SINCE LAST CONTACT WITH OWNER, I HAVE LEFT 3 MESSAGES REQUESTING RECORDS WITH NO REPLY.  THE MECHANIC AT KPIM HAS INFORMED ME THAT THE EDDY CURRENT INSPECTION HAS BEEN COMPLETED AND THAT HE WAS GOING TO BE HIRED TO INSTALL A NEW DOOR.    AS OF 12/08/2015 THE AIRCRAFT IS STILL PARKED AT KPIM.  I AM AWAITING RECORDS TO DETERMINE IF AD89-03-04 HAS BEEN COMPLETED.  THIS IS A CABIN DOOR AD FOR INSTALL OF A DOOR ADJAR WARNING LIGHT.  DUE TO LACK OF CORRESPONDANCE, I AM SENDING A LETTER REQUESTING AIRCRAFT/AIRMAN RECORDS TO THE OWNER ON 12/14/2015.  I WAS CONTACTED ON 12/14/2015 AND WAS PROVIDED EVERTHING THAT I REQUESTED SO I RECINDED THE LETTER.  THE DOOR AD WAS COMPLIED WITH ON 1/29/1990. I PROVIDED A SPECIAL FLIGHT PERMIT ON 12/15/2015 TO HEADLAND, AL FOR MAINTENANCE COMPLETION AT AEROSTAR WORLD INC.  A TEMPORARY LOANER DOOR WAS INSTALLED FOR THE FERRY FLIGHT AND LIMITATIONS WERE ADDED.  THE AIRCRAFT DOOR STRUCTURE RECEIVED AN EDDY CURRENT INSPECTION BY SPACE SCIENCE SERVICES, INC. ON 12/23/2015.  NO CRACK INDICATIONS WERE NOTED.  AEROSTAR WORLD, INC. COMPLETED THE INSTALLATION OF A SERVICEABLE DOOR ON 1/26/2016. I CONTACTED AEROSTAR AIRCRAFT CORPORATION AND THEY PROVIDED ME WITH INSTALLATION AND ADJUSTMENT PUBLICATIONS FOR THE DOOR ADJAR WARNING SWITCH. THE TECH PUB STATES THAT ADJUSTMENT OF THE DOOR BOLT PIN MAY BE REQUIRED FOR PROPER OPERATION.    THE PILOTS WRITTEN STATEMENT SAYS ?HE NOTICED THE PILOT DOOR LEVER WAS NOT IN PARALLEL POSITION AND THEN THE LIGHT ILLUMINATED?.  THIS INDICATES THE DOOR MAY HAVE BEEN OUT OF ADJUSTMENT ENOUGH TO CAUSE AN ALLEGED ERRONEOUS INDICATION.  BECAUSE THE ORIGINAL DOOR WAS LOST AND THE REPLACEMENT DOOR IS A DIFFERENT DOOR THAT HAD TO BE RIGGED, THERE IS NO WAY OF KNOWING FOR SURE IF THE DOOR WARNING SYSTEM WAS FUNCTIONING PROPERLY AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT. THEREFORE, I AM MARKING NO TO AIRWORTHINESS ON THE FAA FORM 8020-23.  THE PILOTS WRITTEN STATEMENT SAYS THAT THE ?DOOR LEVER WAS NOT IN PARALLEL POSITION?, THIS SUGGEST THAT THE DOOR HANDLE WAS NOT FULLY LOCKED. THEREFORE, I AM MARKING YES TO AIRMAN COMPETENCE ON THE FAA FORM 8020-23.

EVIDENCE OF AMPLE FUEL ON BOARD WAS A LARGE FLASH FIRE BURN AREA AND INTENSE FIRE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. EXAMINATION OF THE FUEL VALVE BY A BEECHCRAFT ACCIDENT INVESTIGATOR SHOWED THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS IN THE LEFT MAIN TANK POSITION. RESULTS OF THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED CONFUSION ON THE RAMP.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS INITIALLY USING A DIGITAL GUIDANCE PARKING SYSTEM FOR SELF-PARKING BUT SIMULTANEOUSLY WAS BEING MARSHALLED-IN BY SOMEONE WITH NO WANDS.  IN ADDITION, A WING WALKER WAS STATIONED ON THE RIGHT WING WITH LIGHTED WANDS, WHILE ANOTHER WING WALKER WAS STATIONED BY THE LEFT WING AND NEAR THE DEICE TRUCK WITH NO WANDS. IT WAS OBVIOUS FROM REVIEWING THE VIDEO AND INTERVIEWING THE CAPTAIN THAT COMMUNICATION BETWEEN GROUND PERSONNEL WAS DEFICIENT. WHEN THE AIRCRAFTS LEFT WINGTIP WAS APPROACHING THE DEICING TRUCK AND A COLLISION WAS IMMINENT, THE WING WALKER HID BEHINDTHE DEICING TRUCK.  EVEN AFTER THE WINGTIP STRUCK THE DEICING TRUCK, THE LEAD MARSHALLER WAS STILL SIGNALING THE AIRCRAFT FORWARD.  THE WEATHER CONDITIONS AT THE TIME WERE POOR, WITH SNOW AND SLEET.  SNOW, SLUSH, AND ICE COVERED THE GROUND AND RAMP SAFETY AREA MARKINGS.  THE LEAD-IN LINE HAD BEEN SHOVELED.   ANY FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS OR CORRECTIVE ACTIONS ARE DEFERRED TO THE AMERICAN AIRLINES CMO.  RECOMMENDATION:  REVIEW GROUND OPERATION MARSHALLING PROCEDURES.  TURN OFF THE DIGITAL GUIDANCE PARKING SYSTEM WHEN MARSHLERS ARE GUIDING AIRCRAFT.

N201KY LOST ALL POWER ON THE BASE-TO-FINAL TURN, AND WAS LINED UP WITH A RESIDENTIAL STREET. N201KY, WHILE ATTEMPTING TO LAND, STRUCK PARKED CARS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE STREET, WITH THE LEFT AND RIGHT AIRCRAFT WING TIPS SCRUBBING OFF AIRSPEED, AND SLIDING DOWN THE STREET SPRAYING FUEL, ALONG THE LENGTH OF THE STREET. N201KY CAME TO REST TWENTY FEET FROM AN APARTMENT COMPLEX, WITH A LARGE GROUP OF CHILDREN PLAYING IN THE PARKING LOT.  NO ONE ON THE GROUND WAS INJURED, AND THE PILOT EXITED THE AIRCRAFT UNHARMED. THE PILOT, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, THE LONE OCCUPANT OF N201KY, WAS INTERVIEWED, AND PROVIDED A HANDWRITTEN STATEMENT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ WAS ASKED TO PRESENT HIS MEDICAL CERTIFICATE AND AIRCRAFT REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE. HE WAS UNABLE TO LOCATE HIS MEDICAL CERTIFICATE, AND STATED THE AIRCRAFT REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE WAS AT HIS HOME, IN HIS SAFE.  THE WRECKAGE OF N201KY, WITH FUEL STILL ONBOARD, CLOSE TO THE POSITION OF THE STILL OCCUPIED APARTMENT BUILDING, FULL OF CHILDREN, WAS A CONCERN TO THE FAA IIC. THE NTSB WAS CONTACTED FOR AN ETA OF THE RECOVERY TEAM. THE NTSB CONTACT ON THE EAST COAST STATED THAT IT WOULD TAKE EIGHT HOURS FOR THE RECOVERY TEAM TO ARRIVE FROM PHOENIX, AZ. THIS TIMEFRAME WAS NOT FEASIBLE, DUE TO THE FACT THAT LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT AND FIRE DEPARTMENT RESOURCES WERE UNABLE TO REMAIN ON THE SITE FOR THE EIGHT HOURS IT WOULD TAKE FOR THE NTSB RECOVERY TEAM TO ARRIVE, DUE TO OTHER PUBLIC DEMAND FOR THEIR SERVICES.  THE PILOT, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, WAS HAVING DIFFICULTY CONTACTING HIS INSURANCE COMPANY. THUS, A REQUEST FOR A FUEL TRUCK TO PERFORM DEFUELING SERVICE ON N201KY WAS MADE TO THE WHITEMAN AIRPORT. A FUEL TRUCK WAS UNAVAILABLE TO PERFORM THIS SERVICE.  WITH NO SUPPORT FROM THE NTSB, A MEETING WAS CALLED BY THE FAA IIC WITH LAPD AND LAFD. THE FIRST CONCERN WAS OPENING A ROUTE OUT OF THE ACCIDENT SITE TO PROVIDE THE RESIDENTS STRANDED BEHIND THE SITE A MEANS TO LEAVE THE SITE IN ORDER TO PICK THEIR CHILDREN UP FROM SCHOOL. THE SECOND CONCERN WAS THE DEFUELING OF N201KY, AND THE REMOVAL OF THE AIRCRAFT FROM THE AREA TO A SAFE AND SECURE STORAGE LOCATION.  THE LAFD FIRE CAPTAIN RECOMMENDED FILLING THE LEFT WING, WHICH STILL CONTAINED FUEL, WITH WATER TO DISPLACE THE FUMES IN THE TANK, ALLOWING THE HIGH SPEED CUTTING OF THE AIRFRAME SAFER, PREVENTING FUEL IGNITION BY THE SPARKS GENERATED BY THE CUTTING WHEEL. SUBSEQUENTLY, THE LEFT WING WAS FILLED WITH WATER, AND THE AIRFRAME WAS CUT.  DUE TO THE DARKNESS OF EVENING, AND THE LATE HOUR, PARTIES DISCUSSED AND INITIATED UTILIZING THE LAPD CONTRACT IMPOUND YARD TO STORE THE AIRCRAFT OVERNIGHT. USE OF THE LAPD IMPOUND YARD WAS THE MOST EXPEDIENT METHOD OF CLEARING THE STREET OF THE WRECKAGE, AND SECURING THE AIRCRAFT FOR FURTHER INSPECTION. TWO FLATBED TOW TRUCKS FROM THE LAPD YARD ARRIVED TO REMOVE THE AIRCRAFT WRECKAGE. THE HIGH LEVEL OF COOPERATION BETWEEN THE LAPD, LAFD, AND THE FAA WAS INSTRUMENTAL IN THE SUCCESSFUL OUTCOME TO THIS HIGHLY VOLATILE SITUATION IN THE LOCAL COMMUNITY OF PACOIMA, CA.  AN ENGINE RUN AND TEARDOWN INSPECTION WILL BE CONDUCTED BY THE NTSB AND THE FAA IIC ON 03/14/2016.

THEY WERE NOT ALLOWED TO TAKE THE PARACHUTE, PER THE FAA, AND IT HAD ALREADY BEEN COLLECTED BY SOMEONE AND LOCKED IN ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ LOCKER ALONG WITH HIS HELMET CAMERA.   SKY DIVE DELAND OWNER ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ARRIVED DURING THE INVESTIGATION AND BECAME VERY CONFRONTATIONAL. HE STATED HE HAS TALKED TO THE FSDO 15 MANAGER ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, AND SHE STATED THE POLICE HAVE NO RIGHT TO COLLECT THE CHUTE WHEN THIS TYPE OF INCIDENT OCCURS.   SGT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ CALLED THE ROC, WHO CONTACTED ME. I WAS PLACED ON A THREE WAY CONVERSATION WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ AND SGT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ WAS TALKING OVER US CONTINUOUSLY.   I EXPLAINED TO ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^AND THE SGT. WHEN A SKYDIVER IS INVOLVED IN AN ACCIDENT, THE FIRST STEP BY THE FAA IS TO DETERMINE IF ANY REGULATIONS WERE VIOLATED. THE FAA WILL EXAMINE THE CIRCUMSTANCES AND ROUTE OF THE FLIGHT; THE CERTIFICATION OF THE PILOT; THE AIRWORTHINESS OF THE AIRCRAFT; AND WILL ENSURE THAT THE PARACHUTES WERE PACKED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE REGULATIONS.  IF THE FAA DOES NOT FIND ANY EVIDENCE OF REGULATORY VIOLATION, IT WILL DEFER ANY FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE ACCIDENT TO LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT. THE ACCIDENT THEN BECOMES A LAW ENFORCEMENT INVESTIGATION, AND THE FAA HAS NO FURTHER INVOLVEMENT.  IF THE FAA DETERMINES ONE OR MORE OF THE REGULATIONS WERE VIOLATED, IT WILL LAUNCH A SEPARATE INVESTIGATION INTO THE AREAS UNDER ITS REGULATORY CONTROL, WHICH CONCERN THE AIRCRAFT, ITS PILOT, MECHANIC, THE LOCATION OR TIMING OF THE JUMP, AND THE PARACHUTE RIGGING.  THE OWNER EXPRESSED SOME DISSATISFACTION WITH MY EXPLANATION; BUT THE POLICE SGT. WAS ABLE TO RETRIEVE THE PARACHUTE.

ALMOST INSTANTLY THE WHEELS WERE CAUGHT BY THE GRASS AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS SLAMMED TO THE GROUND CAUSING SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO THE FUSELAGE. THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO EVACUATE HIMSELF AND THE PASSENGER SAFELY. ALL AERODYNAMIC CONTROL SURFACES ACCOUNTED FOR IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY OF THE FUSELAGE EXCEPT THE LEFT ELEVATOR(A THOROUGH DEBRIS FIELD SURVEY WAS NOT CONDUCTED AT DUE TO TIME CONSTRAINTS). THE THREE BLADE CONSTANT SPEED PROPELLER AND ONE UNDAMAGED BLADE AND TWO BLADES BENT AFT MIDSPAN, AND THERE IS NO APPARENT LEADING EDGE DAMAGE TO ANY PROP BLADE. THE ENGINE COULD NOT BE EVALUATED DO TO WRECKAGE CONDITION AND ORIENTATION. THE CP TELEPHONED THE COMPANY DISPATCHER LOCATED IN BETHEL, AK (BET) TO FIND OUT THE LOCATION OF N91170. THE COMPANY DISPATCHER COULD NOT CONFIRM THE EXACT LOCATION, BUT TOLD THE CP THAT HE HAD RECEIVED A TEXT MESSAGE FROM THE PILOT OF N91170 AT 1018 AST (1818 GMT), AND AT THAT TIME THE AIRCRAFT WAS LOCATED AT AQH. THE CP AND COMPANY DISPATCHER AGREED THAT THE CP WOULD TAKE THE WAITING PASSENGER TO AQH AND SEARCH FOR N91170 ALONG THE ROUTE. THE CP DEPARTED GNU AT ABOUT 1125 AST (1925 GMT) AND ARRIVED AT AQH AT 1155 AST (1955 GMT). THE COMPANY DISPATCHER AND CP COORDINATED A SEARCH EFFORT. TWO OTHER AIRCRAFT WERE DISPATCHED FROM BETHEL TO SEARCH FOR THE MISSING AIRPLANE. N91170 WAS LOCATED BY THE SEARCH PARTY AT APPROXIMATELY1300 AST (2100 GMT). AN ALASKA NATIONAL GUARD HELICOPTER WAS DISPATCHED TO RETRIEVE THE INJURED PILOT. PHOTOGRAPHS OF THE ACCIDENT SCENE WERE OBTAINED FROM THECOMPANY. THE PHOTOGRAPHS SHOWED N91170 SUBSTANTIALLY DAMAGED ON A STEEP HILLSIDE. THE MAJORITY OF THE WRECKAGE WAS CENTRALLY LOCATED WHERE THE AIRPLANE CAME TO REST. ONE PHOTOGRAPH SHOWED SIGNIFICANT GROUND SCORING DOWNSLOPE OF THE WRECKAGE. BASED ON THE PHOTOGRAPHS, THE ROUTE OF FLIGHT APPEARS TO HAVE BEEN INTO THE DIRECTION OF RISING TERRAIN.  ON JUNE 19, 2016, A NATIONAL TRANSPORTATION SAFETY BOARD (NTSB) INVESTIGATOR INTERVIEWED THE PILOT AT THE ALASKA NATIVE MEDICAL CENTER IN ANCHORAGE, AK. THE PILOT TOLD THE INVESTIGATOR THAT HE ESTIMATED THE CEILING TO BE ABOUT 800 FT. AND HE WAS IN CRUISE FLIGHT AT 700 FT. AFTER DEPARTING AQH, HE WAS TRYING TO WIND HIS WAY THROUGH THE BACKSIDE OF A MOUNTAIN PASS. HE TRIED TO CUT ACROSS THE MOUNTAINS THROUGH A DRAW HE THOUGHT WENT THROUGH. WHILE MANEUVERING THROUGH THE CANYON, HE CAME TO AN AREA THAT WAS TOO NARROW AND STEEP TO SAFELY TURN AROUND. HE INITIATED A CLIMB INTO THE CLOUDS AND ATTEMPTED TO TURN AROUND. DURING THE TURN AND STILL IN THE CLOUDS, THE AIRPLANE IMPACTED THE TERRAIN.  COPIES OF PILOT TRAINING RECORDS OBTAINED FROM THE COMPANY SHOWED THE PILOT WAS PROPERLY CERTIFICATED; HELD A CURRENT MEDICAL CERTIFICATE; CURRENT AND QUALIFIED FOR THE FLIGHT CONDUCTED.  ON JUNE 22, 2016 AN FAA INSPECTOR FROM ANCHORAGE, AK TRAVELED TO BET TO EXAMINE MAINTENANCE RECORDS FOR N91170. THE INSPECTION STATUS OF N91170 WAS FOUND TO BE CURRENT AND IN COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL AVIATION REGULATIONS. THE RECORDS ALSO SHOWED AN EMERGENCY LOCATOR BEACON (ELT) WAS INSTALLED ON THE AIRCRAFT, HOWEVER, NO SIGNAL FROM THE ELT WAS REPORTED FOLLOWING THE ACCIDENT. ON JUNE 29, 2016, THE PILOT CONTACTED THE FAA IIC BY TELEPHONE FROM A MEDICAL FACILITY LOCATED IN COLORADO, USA. DURING THE TELEPHONE CONVERSATION THE PILOT CONFIRMED THE CONTENT AND ACCURACY OF THE INFORMATION OBTAINED BY THE NTSB INVESTIGATOR DURING THE INTERVIEW ON JUNE 19, 2016.

THE FOLLOWING POSITIONS WERE IDENTIFIED DURING THE TRAINING:  1.   THE SYSTEM OPERATOR (SO) (FIREMAN/DECEASED) OPERATES THE WINCH DEVISE AND EVENTUALLY DIRECTS THE AIRCRAFT TO THE SITE, ONCE PILOT LOSES VISUAL CONTACT. 2.  RESCUE SPECIALIST (RS) DELAWARE STATE POLICE: IS THE PARAMEDIC THAT IS HOISTED DOWN TO SITE. 3.  PILOT (DELAWARE STATE POLICE): PIC OF AIRCRAFT AND OPERATES THE HELICOPTER. 4.  SAFETY OFFICER (FIREMAN): ALTHOUGH NOT REQUIRED DURING AN ACTUAL EMERGENCY FLIGHT, THE DELAWARE STATE POLICE DOES REQUIRE THE SAFETY OFFICER DURING ALL TRAINING MISSIONS. ACTS AS A "THIRD SET OF EYES" FOR ALL SAFETY ISSUES. EACH CREW MEMBER PERFORMING THE DUTIES LISTED ABOVE ARE SECURED TO THE AIRCRAFT BY RESTRAINTS FITTED TO ATTACHING POINTS INSTALLED ON THE AIRCRAFT.  EACH PERSON WAS TO SWITCH POSITIONS DURING THE TRAINING MISSION. THERE ARE APPROXIMATELY 3-4 HOISTING EVOLUTIONS COMPLETED FOR EACH OF THE CREW MEMBERS. DURING THE FINAL TRAINING PHASE, BUT THE FIRST EVOLUTION AS THE SO. THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED. INSPECTION OF THE RESTRAINT SYSTEM, TETHER STRAPS, AND HOOKS SHOWED NO DAMAGE OR FAILURE OF ANY KIND. CHECK LISTS WERE USED DURING ACTUAL AND TRAINING MISSIONS.  THESE CHECK LISTS INCLUDE CHECKING THE RESTRAIN SYSTEMS AND TETHERING OF EACH CREW MEMBER TWO TIMES BEFORE THE ACTUAL HOISTING TAKES PLACE.  ALTHOUGH THERE IS DOCUMENTED TRAINING FOR HOIST TRAINING WHICH IS AN EXTERNAL LOAD OPERATION, THIS PUBLIC AIRCRAFT OPERATION (PAO) DOES NOT HAVE A ROTORCRAFT LOAD COMBINATION FLIGHT MANUAL (RLCFM) WHICH WOULD INCORPORATE A MULTITUDE OF POLICIES, PROCEDURES AND WEIGHT AND BALANCE INFORMATION, TO NAME A FEW.  THIS RLCFM IS APPROVED BY THE FAA.  COUNSELING CAN BE ACCOMPLISHED TO DISCUSS THE PROPER DEVELOPMENT OF A RLCFM AND AUTHORIZATION OF A EXTERNAL LOAD OPERATING CERTIFICATE.

ALTHOUGH SMALL IN SIZE, THE LEAK IS SUFFICIENT TO HAVE PREVENTED THE SYSTEM FROM REACHING FULL OPERATING PRESSURE AND THUS PREVENTING THE NOSE LANDING GEAR FROM REACHING THE FULL FORWARD/LOCK POSITION IN FLIGHT. IT APPEARS A MECHANICAL FAULT OF THE BETA BACK UP SYSTEM OCCURRED PRIOR TO DEPARTURE.  EVIDENCE OF THE MECHANICAL FAULT WAS THE CONTINUOUS ILLUMINATION OF THE NO. 2 PROPELLER  GROUND RANGE ADVISORY LIGHT WITH POWER LEVERS ADVANCE BEYOND THE FLIGHT IDLE POSITION FOR TAKEOFF.     ALTHOUGH THE AIRCRAFT'S MECHANICAL CONDITION WAS COMPROMISED IT APPEARS THE FLIGHT CREW SHOULD HAVE ABORTED THE TAKEOFF PER COMMUTAIR STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS MANUAL (AOM) REVISION 17, EFFECTIVE 10/14/15, PARAGRAPH 03.40 TAKEOFF STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: CAUTION: IF THE #1 OR #2 PROPELLER GROUND RANGE ADVISORY LIGHTS ILLUMINATE THE TAKEOFF MUST BE ABORTED.     AOM PARAGRAPH 03.40 CAUTION ORIGINATED FROM AN APRIL 1, 2014 BOMBARDIER REVISION DUE TO A POTENTIAL CONCERN WITH PROPELLER CONTROL UNITS REPAIRED/OVERHAULED BY PACIFIC  PROPELLER INTERNATIONAL, LLC.     THE CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT TEAM (CMT) OBTAINED ATC AUDIO FOR THE EVENT.  INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE FIRST APPROACH ATTEMPT TO KIAD RUNWAY 1L WAS DISCONTINUED DUE TO THE LANDING GEAR FAILING TO EXTEND. AFTER DELAY VECTORS THE FLIGHT CREW WAS ABLE TO  EXTEND THE LANDING GEAR AND COMMENCE APPROACH TERMINATING IN A SAFE LANDING. FLIGHT CREW INABILITY TO EXTEND THE LANDING GEAR APPEARS TO BE THE RESULT OF FAILING TO PERFORM A REQUIRED EMERGENCY CHECKLIST ITEM IN THE PROPER SEQUENCE.     THE FLIGHT CREW STATED THEY DID NOT SEE THE ADVISORY LIGHT - BLUE & WHITE IN COLOR ILLUMINATED. A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR MAY HAVE BEEN THE SETTING SUN DIRECTLY IN FRONT OF THE RUNWAY 30 DEPARTURE.     BOTH FLIGHT CREWMEMBER REPORTS WERE ACCEPTED INTO THE FLIGHT CREWMEMBER ASAP PROGRAM.  FLIGHT CREWMEMBER REMEDIAL TRAINING HAS OCCURRED. ADDITIONALLY, JJBA HAS COMMITTED TO IMPLEMENTING A NEW SOP TO ENSURE ADVISORY LIGHTS ARE EXTINGUISHED PRIOR TO DEPARTURE.  ADDITIONAL SAFETY ENHANCEMENTS HAVE BEEN RECOMMEND BY THE CMU WHICH WILL BE TRACKED TO COMPLETION.

THERE WAS NO CLEVIS PIN OR SAFETY COTTER PIN FOUND IN THE GEAR WELL AREA. FURTHER DISCUSSION WITH THE OWNER REVEALED THAT THIS AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN SITTING FOR ALMOST 20 YEARS (MOTHBALLED) AND RECENTLY HAD BEEN RETURNED TO SERVICE AFTER AN ANNUAL INSPECTION ON MAY 27, 2016. EXTENSIVE MAINTENANCE HAD BEEN PERFORMED TO THE AIRCRAFT FOR THE INSPECTION. MAINTENANCE RECORDS INDICATE A GEAR RETRACTION SYSTEM WAS SERVICED AND RETRACTION/EXTENSION TEST WAS PERFORMED SEVERAL TIMES USING A HYDRAULIC MULE AS WELL AS THE A/C EMERGENCY HAND PUMP. ALL GEAR CYCLES PERFORMED NORMALLY WITH NO HYDRAULIC LEAKS INDICATED. OTHER THAN REPLACEMENT OF LANDING GEAR HOSES, NO OTHER MAINTENANCE WAS PERFORMED ON THE GEAR SYSTEM DURING THE INSPECTION. THE OWNER STATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD FLOWN SEVERAL TIMES SINCE THE ANNUAL INSPECTION AND NO RETRACTION PROBLEMS HAD OCCURRED PRIOR TO THIS FLIGHT. THE OWNER AND HIS SON WERE ABOARD THE AIRCRAFT ON THIS FLIGHT. THE AIRCRAFT HAS FLOWN 8.45 HOURS SINCE THE LAST ANNUAL INSPECTION.

AFTER MAKING A NORMAL LANDING AT THE WEST END OF UGANIK LAKE AND UNLOADING THE MECHANICS AND TOOLS THE PILOT TAXIED EASTBOUND ON THE LAKE APPROXIMATELY 3800 FEET TO THE AREA NEAR THE NORTH SHORELINE THAT WOULD ALLOW FOR A TAKEOFF WESTBOUND DOWN THE UGANIK RIVER. THIS WOULD BE THE NORMAL TAKEOFF AND DEPARTURE ROUTE FROM UGANIK LAKE TO AMOOK ISLAND.   AT ABOUT 1125 LOCAL TIME THE PILOT STARTED HIS TAKEOFF RUN WESTBOUND TOWARDS THE RIVER OUTFLOW AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS SEEN TO LIFT OFF OF THE LAKE AND START A CLIMB. AS THE BEAVER PASSED OVER THE WITNESSES THE ENGINE WAS HEARD TO BE OPERATING NORMALLY AT TAKEOFF POWER.  THEY STATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT CLIMBED OVER THE END OF THE LAKE, WHERE THEY WERE STANDING, AT AN ALTITUDE OF APPROXIMATELY 100 TO 200 FEET AND THEN INSTEAD OF CONTINUING WESTBOUND OUT THE RIVER AS WOULD BE EXPECTED IT WAS SEEN TO START A LEFT HAND TURN AS IF THE PILOT WAS ATTEMPTING TO TURN EASTBOUND TO AVOID INCREASING TERRAIN.  THIS TURN INCREASED IN RATE AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS SEEN TO BEGIN TO LOSE ALTITUDE.  THE LEFT BANK INCREASED AS DID THE RATE OF DESCENT UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT IMPACTED THE LAKE ABOUT 100 FEET FROM SHORE AND IN 4 FEET OF WATER.  THE CRASH SITE WAS ON THE SOUTH SHORELINE OF THE LAKE ABOUT 200 YARDS TO THE SOUTH OF THE WITNESSES.  REDEMPTION AIR?S CHIEF PILOT COMMANDEERED A RAFT AND PADDLED ACROSS THE LAKE TO THE CRASH SITE AND BEGAN A RECOVERY EFFORT TO REMOVE THE PASSENGERS AND PILOT FROM THE PARTLY SUNKEN AIRCRAFT. SHE PROCEEDED TO TAXI ONTO THE RUNWAY AND THE TAXIWAY WHERE THE AIRCRAFT FINALLY CAME TO A FULL STOP DUE TO A COLLAPSED LEFT MAIN GEAR. THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES.  INSPECTORS FROM SW17 INTERVIEWED THE AIRMAN AND HER INSTRUCTOR. DURING THE INTERVIEW SEVERAL ITEMS OF INTEREST EMERGED.  THESE ARE AS FOLLOWS:  -CTC DOESN'T EMPHASIZE AIRCRAFT SPEEDS. WHEN THE INSPECTORS ASKED INSTRUCTOR TO DESCRIBE HOW TO TEACH A LANDING/TRAFFIC PATTERN, THE INSTRUCTOR DESCRIBED PROCEDURES BUT NO AIRSPEED. WHEN ASKED ABOUT THIS OMISSION, HE ADMITTED THE SCHOOL EMPHASIZED MORE ON VISUAL CUES THAN AIRSPEED. THE ONLY RANGE HE ACTUALLY PROVIDED WILLINGLY WAS TO HAVE STUDENTS BE WITHIN THE WHITE ARC/FLAP LIMITATION SPEED. WHEN PUSHED TO GIVE A DESIRED TOLERANCE, HE GAVE A SPEED OF "APPROXIMATELY 70-80 KNOTS ON BASE AND 75-80 ON FINAL FOR THE PIPER." WHEN CROSS-REFERENCED WITH THE AIRCRAFT'S POH, THE SPEEDS ARE SLIGHTLY OFF. THE AIRMAN'S LAST AIRSPEED CHECK ON FINAL WAS 70 KNOTS WITH 20? OF FLAPS, SLOWER THAN THEN INSTRUCTOR'S SPEED RANGE, BUT ABOVE THE AIRCRAFT'S FINAL APPROACH SPEED OF 66 KNOTS AS PER THE POH.  -CTC TEACHES POWER-OFF LANDINGS AS THE NORMAL LANDING, WITH THE RUNWAY NUMBERS AS THE AIM POINT. THIS PROVIDES NO SAFETY BUFFER TO PREVENT OFF-RUNWAY LANDINGS. THIS ALSO MAKES IT MORE DIFFICULT FOR STUDENTS TO LEARN THE FAA'S DEFINITION OF A STABILIZED APPROACH.   -CTC DOESN'T REQUIRE WEIGHT AND BALANCE CALCULATIONS IF FLIGHT IS IN THE LOCAL AREA.   -THE AIRMAN'S INSTRUCTOR IS THE ASSISTANT CHIEF FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR.  -CTC DOESN'T EXCLUSIVELY USE FITS AS THE GRADING STANDARD. WITHOUT THE GRADING STANDARD, IT IS DIFFICULT TO TRACK WHAT TRAINING LINE ITEMS THE AIRMAN HAS STRUGGLED WITH IN THE PAST, SPECIFICALLY LANDING-RELATED LINE ITEMS.   THESE ITEMS ARE INDICATION OF A WEAKENING FLIGHT TRAINING PROGRAM AND HAVE BEEN FORWARDED TO CTC'S POI FOR REVIEW.

THE PILOT THEN PUSHED THE NOSE OVER, SWITCHED FUEL TANKS FROM THE RIGHT TO THE LEFT, TURNED ON THE IGNITERS AND HELD DOWN THE START BUTTON BUT WAS NOT SUCCESSFUL IN RESTARTING THE ENGINE. THE PILOT CALLED ATC DECLARING AN EMERGENCY AND WAS VECTORED BACK TO THE AIRPORT. THE PROP WAS THEN FEATHERED USING THE CONTROL LEVER AND IT CAME TO A COMPLETE STOP. TIME FRAME FROM THE BEGINNING OF THE POWER LOSS EVENT TO THIS POINT WAS ABOUT TWO MINUTES. THE PILOT REALIZED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS LOSING ALTITUDE TOO QUICKLY TO MAKE THE AIRPORT. HE SCANNED FOR AND FOUND AN ALTERNATIVE LANDING FIELD (400 STREET LOCATED ABOUT 5 MILES WEST OF IOLA KS (RUNNING NORTH AND SOUTH)). AN ATTEMPT AT A NORMAL LANDING WAS MADE ON 400 ST. HOWEVER, ACCORDING TO THE PILOT, THE AIRCRAFT CAME IN ?A LITTLE HOT? AND THE TREES ON THE SIDE OF THE ROAD ?GOT TO HIM FASTER THAN HE ANTICIPATED?. AT ABOUT 10 FEET OFF THE GROUND (VERIFIED TO BE ACCURATE BY TREE DAMAGE AT THE SITE) THE AIRCRAFT HIT TREES WITH THE LEFT WINGTIP CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO STEER INTO A LARGE DEAD TREE ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE ROAD. THE PT-6 ENGINE AND PROPELLER BECAME LODGED IN THE TREE AND WERE SUBSEQUENTLY RIPPED FROM THE ENGINE FIREWALL. THE MOMENTUM OF THE AIRFRAME CARRIED  IT 100 FEET FURTHER UP THE ROAD AS IT SPUN 540 DEGREES AND HIT THE GROUND FLAT ON ITS BELLY (NOSE GEAR AND LEFT MAIN GEAR WERE FOUND COLLAPSED WHILE THE RIGHT LANDING GEAR WAS TORN FREE OF THE AIRFRAME). THE AIRCRAFT ENDED UP FACING NEARLY 180 DEGREES FROM THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL (AIRCRAFT NOW POINTING SOUTH). THE 540 DEGREE SPIN RESULTED IN FORCED REMOVAL OF SIGNIFICANT PORTIONS OF BOTH WINGS FROM THE WINGTIPS INBOARD AS WELL AS THE TAIL SECTION (INCLUDING BOTH THE HORIZONTAL AND VERTICAL STABILIZER). THE LANDING GEAR WAS IN THE DOWN POSITION.  THE AIRFRAME SLIDE BACKWARDS ON ITS BELLY AS EVIDENCED BY BROKEN BELLY ANTENNAS AND GROUND SCARRING FOUND ON THE ROAD. THE AIRFRAME CAME TO REST RIGHT SIDE UP. AT LEAST ONE FUEL TANK RUPTURED AS EVIDENCED BY LARGE AMOUNTS OF FUEL DRAINING FROM THE AIRCRAFT. NO AFTER CRASH FIRE OCCURRED. WRECK SITE LOCATION WAS 6.2 MILES WEST AND 2.4 MILES NORTH OF THE ALAN COUNTY AIRPORT.

THE PRIMARY MECHANICAL INDICATOR MOUNTED ON THE FLOOR IS A ROTATING TUBE THAT MOVES THE GEAR TO ITS EXTENDED/RETRACTED POSITIONS. THEREFORE, IF IT INDICATES THE GEAR IS DOWN, THE GEAR IS DOWN. IT?S UNCLEAR WHETHER THE PILOT VERIFIED THIS INDICATOR OR THE AURAL TONE ALL OF WHICH ARE SECONDARY INDICATORS. AS WELL AS A THROTTLE MOUNTED POSITION SWITCH AND AN AIRSPEED SAFETY SWITCH AS THIS WILL ACCURATELY IDENTIFY GEAR STATUS IF, THE SYSTEM IS RIGGED AND ELECTRICAL COMPONENTS IS IN WORKING ORDER. PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION VERIFIED THE GEAR HANDLE IN THE DOWN POSITION; HOWEVER, WHEN THE MASTER SWITCH WAS TURN ON, THE GEAR STILL REMAINED UP. THE GEAR WAS EXTENDED DOWN VIA THE EMERGENCY CRANK. THIS ACTION WAS STATED TO BE PERFORMED MULTIPLE TIMES WITH THE SAME RESULTS. BOTH THE MECHANICAL INDICATOR ON THE FLOOR AND HANDLE ILLUMINATED GREEN. FURTHER EXAMINATION OF THE AIRCRAFT DAMAGE CAN BE DESCRIBED AS MINOR. THE AIRCRAFT INCURRED DAMAGE TO UNDERCARRIAGE SKIN, OR WHAT THEY CALL A ONE PIECE COVER AND HAS SEVERAL HOLES GROUND THROUGH AND CAN BE REPAIRED. THE NOSE DOORS HAD EXTENSIVE DAMAGE; THE AIRCRAFT STEP AND THE TRANSPONDER ANTENNA HAVE GROUND SCARING. THE DEW POINT AND TEMPERATURE SPREAD WAS 1 TO 2 DEGREES INDICATING ICING CONDITIONS.  LOCAL RESIDENTS LIVING BELOW THE CRASH SITE ALSO STATED MOUNTAIN OBSCURATION AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT.   AERONAUTICAL CHARTS FOR VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) FLIGHTS DEPICT A MAXIMUM ELEVATION FIGURE (MEF) OF 8,400 FEET FOR SAFE OBSTACLE CLEARANCE IN THAT QUADRANT. NO FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED AND THE PILOT DID NOT OBTAIN A WEATHER BRIEFING FROM OFFICIAL SOURCES. THE PRIVATE PILOT WAS NOT INSTRUMENT RATED. AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) RADAR DATA SHOWS THAT AFTER DEPARTING SDL THE AIRCRAFT MADE A GRADUAL CLIMB TO AN APPARENT CRUISING ALTITUDE OF 7,200 FEET MSL AND THEN HIGHER TO 7,950 FEET MSL. THIS ALTITUDE DID NOT REMAIN CONSTANT, HOWEVER. SEVERAL TIMES PRIOR TO IMPACT WITH TERRAIN, THE AIRCRAFT DESCENDED FOLLOWED BY A CLIMB, EACH SUBSEQUENT CLIMB LOWER THAN THE ONE BEFORE IT. THESE DESCENTS VARIED FROM A FEW HUNDRED FEET TO AS MUCH AS 1300 FEET. AT NO TIME DID THE PILOT ALTER HIS HEADING.  THE INITIAL IMPACT POINT (IIP) CONSISTED OF A 50 FOOT TALL TREE WHICH TORE ONE OF THE ELEVATORS OFF.  TREES FURTHER UPSLOPE TORE THE WINGS FROM THE FUSELAGE AND 40 FEET BEYOND THE IIP A HEAVY GROUND SCAR WAS OBSERVERD SURROUNDED BY SECTIONS OF THE WINGS, ELEVATORS AND SMALLER AIRPLANE FRAGMENTS AS WELL AS BROKEN BRANCHES AND LOOSE DIRT.  BOTH WINGS HAD BROKEN OFF IMMEDIATELY OUTBOARD OF THE MOUNTING POINTS, THE VERTICAL STABILIZER AND RUDDER WAS SEPARATED FROM THE FUSELAGE EXCEPT BY CONTROL CABLES. EIGHTY FEET BEYOND THE IIP THE FUSELAGE CAME TO REST AT AN UPWARD ANGLE WITH THE ENGINE DETACHED AND LAYING JUST FORWARD OF THE MAIN CABIN. OF THE PROPELLER?S THREE BLADES, TWO WERE STILL ATTACHED TO THE HUB AND ONE WAS RESTING DOWN SLOPE IN THE GROUND SCAR.  THE PROPELLER BLADES DAMAGE WAS CONSISTENT WITH SIGNIFICANT ENGINE POWER AT THE TIME OF IMPACT.

SUBSEQUENT RESEARCH BY MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL DETERMINED THERE WAS A HISTORY  OF FAILURES OF THIS TYPE OF BRASS THROTTLE ARMS. THE FUEL CONTROLLER MANUFACTURER HAD ADDRESSED A FIX TO THIS TYPE OF FAILURE IN A SERVICE BULLETIN (CSB08-03)  IN 2008. THIS BULLETIN CALLS FOR REPLACING THE BRASS ARM WITH A STAINLESS STEEL EQUIVALENT.

AS THE PILOT HAD NOT SELECTED GEAR DOWN HE VERIFIED THAT THE HORN WAS AUDIBLE.  AFTER ADVANCING THE THROTTLES THE PILOT SELECTED THE GEAR LEVER TO THE DOWN POSITION AND PUT IN 10 DEGREES OF FLAPS.  AFTER COMPLETING A BASE LEG TURN FOR THE LANDING RUNWAY, THE PILOT SELECTED 20 DEGREES OF FLAPS.  WHILE ON FINAL APPROACH THE PILOT SELECTED 35 DEGREES OF FLAPS WHICH WAS THE FINAL FLAP SETTING THAT WAS TO BE USED FOR THE LANDING.  THE PILOT DOES NOT RECALL NOR CAN HE VERIFY THAT HE CHECKED THE GREEN GEAR INDICATOR LIGHT TO CONFIRM THAT THE GEAR WAS DOWN AND LOCKED.  HOWEVER, HE DOES DISTINCTLY REMEMBER BRINING THE THROTTLES BACK TO IDLE WHILE ON THE FINAL APPROACH LEG AND HE DID NOT HEAR THE GEAR WARNING HORN.  THE GEAR WARNING HORN IN THIS AIRCRAFT IS DESIGNED TO BE AUDIBLE WHEN THE GEAR IS NOT PHYSICALLY DOWN AND THE THROTTLES ARE REDUCED TO IDLE.  THE ABSENCE OF THE GEAR WARNING HORN THAT THE PILOT NOTED LED HIM TO BELIEVE THAT THE GEAR WAS INDEED DOWN AND LOCKED.  THE PILOT TOUCHED DOWN ON THE RUNWAY JUST BEYOND THE RUNWAY NUMBERS.  AFTER THE TOUCH DOWN THE PILOT CLAIMED THAT THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO SETTLE MORE THEN HE WAS USED TO.  SHORTLY AFTER THIS OBSERVATION BOTH PROPS BEGAN TO STRIKE THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  ALTHOUGH THE FUSELAGE HAD YET TO MAKE CONTACT WITH THE RUNWAY THE PILOT ELECTED TO INDUCE A LEFT TURN TO EXIT THE RUNWAY INTO THE FLAT GRASS AREA ADJACENT TO THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  HE DID THIS FEARING THAT SPARKS CREATED BY THE SKIN OF THE AIRCRAFT AND THE ASPHALT WOULD CREATE A POTENTIAL FOR FIRE.  AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS APPROXIMATELY 20 YARDS INTO THE GRASS AREA THE AIRCRAFT?S FUSELAGE MADE CONTACT WITH THE SURFACE.  THIS IS EVIDENCED BY BOTH MAIN GEAR DOORS AS WELL AS A DISTANCE MEASURING BEACON BEING SHEARED FROM THE BODY OF THE AIRCRAFT.  THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED ANOTHER APPROXIMATELY 10 YARDS BEFORE COMING TO A FULL STOP.   THE PILOT IMMEDIATELY SECURED THE AIRCRAFT AND MADE AND EXIT TO ASSESS WHAT HAD JUST HAPPENED.  AFTER SEVERAL MINUTES THAT PILOT ELECTED TO RETURN TO THE INTERIOR OF THE AIRCRAFT AND CHECK THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS TO SEE IF ANY OF THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS HAD POPPED OUT.  HE NOTED THAT THE GEAR MOTOR CIRCUIT BREAKER HAD INDEED POPPED.  THIS WOULD BE CONSISTENT WITH THE GEAR MOTOR ATTEMPTING TO MOVE THE GEAR TO THE DOWN AND LOCKED POSITION AS IT BEGAN TO COLLAPSE DURING THE LANDING ROLL-OUT.   NO INJURIES WERE SUSTAINED BY THE PILOT.  THE PILOT ATTESTS THAT THERE WERE NO WEATHER PHENOMENA OR ABNORMAL RUNWAY CONDITIONS THAT WOULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THIS EVENT.

AIRCRAFT EVACUATED WITH NO INJURIES TO CREW OR PASSENGERS AND FIRE DID NOT CONTINUE AFTER SHUTDOWN OF ELECTRICAL SYSTEM.   FOLLOW UP INVESTIGATION FOUND THE MOSFET CONTACTORS ABOVE BATTERY IN AFT FUSELAGE HAD CAUGHT FIRE AND MELTED.  DAMAGE FOUND TO WIRING NEAR MOSFET COMPONENT RACK, AND LARGE AMOUNT OF SOOT VISIBLE ON METAL ABOVE THE 4 MOSFETS INSTALLED.  2 OF THE 4 MOSFET CONTACTORS APPEARED VERY DAMAGED WITH MOLTEN METAL FOUND BY ONE UNIT.   RH ELEVATOR HEATER HORN ALSO SEVERELY DAMAGED BY OVERHEATING.  PILOTS REPORTED AIRCRAFT HAD FLOWN THE NIGHT BEFORE AND THAT THE ENGINE NACELLE HEAT HAD BEEN TURNED ON DUE TO ICING CONCERNS ON APPROACH.  BOTH CREWMEMBERS SAID THEY DID NOT TURN ON THE H STAB DEICE HEAT SYSTEM SWITCH THE NIGHT BEFORE THIS EVENT, OR ENGAGE IT DURING STARTUP OF ENGINES THE DAY OF THE FIRE.    HOWEVER, A CONFLICTING NARRATIVE OF THESE EVENTS WAS PROVIDED TO FAA BY A PERSON PRESENT AT THIS FIRE EVENT.  THE REPORTER SAID THAT THE PIC TOLD HIM IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE FIRE THAT THE H STAB DEICE SYSTEM WAS TURNED ON IN FLIGHT THE NIGHT BEFORE AND TURNED OFF AGAIN AFTER A FAIL WARNING LIGHT CAME ON FOR THE H STAB DEICE HEAT SYSTEM.  ADDITIONAL NARRATIVE AMENDMENT 1: COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER DOWNLOAD OBTAINED AND REVIEWED BY FSDO ON 4/21/17.  CVR RECORDING OF CONVERSATIONS BETWEEN PILOT AND COPILOT FROM FLIGHT TO HIO ON MARCH 8 AND ON MORNING OF DEPARTURE PREPARATION ON MARCH 9 SHOW CLEARLY THAT H STAB DEICE SYSTEM WAS USED ON MARCH 8 AND FAILED IN FLIGHT.  NARRATIVE SHOWS THAT BOTH PILOTS DISCUSSED THE FAILURE WARNING LIGHT FOR THE H STAB DEICE SYSTEM THAT CAME ON THE NIGHT BEFORE, AND DID NOT REALIZE THAT THE ELECTRICAL SYSTEM FAULTS DISPLAYING ON MARCH 9 PRIOR TO TAXI WERE CAUSED BY H STAB DEICE SYSTEM FAILURE.    DURING SEVERAL MINUTES OF TROUBLESHOOTING DISCUSSION CVR RECORDING SHOWS BATTERY AND GENERATOR ISSUES WERE SUSPECTED OF CAUSING FAILURE WARNING LIGHTS AND OTHER ANOMALIES, UNTIL THE ENTIRE ELECTRICAL SYSTEM WENT OFF LINE DUE TO MASSIVE ELECTRICAL SHORT IN MOSFET UNITS.  DISCUSSION WITH PILOTS AFTER EVENT FOUND THAT NEITHER OF THEM KNEW ABOUT OR HAD FOLLOWED THE AFM EMERGENCY CHECKLIST FOR H STAB ICE FAIL LIGHT INDICATION, AND THAT THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FOR THE H STAB DEICE SYSTEM CONTROL WAS NOT PULLED BEFORE SHUTTING OFF THE SWITCH AS REQUIRED BY THE AFM CHECKLIST.  PILOT ACTION OF SHUTTING OFF THE SWITCH WITHOUT FIRST PULLING THE H STAB DEICE CONTROL C/B AFTER A WARNING FAIL LIGHT CAME ON SET THE CONDITIONS WHICH COULD LEAD TO A MOSFET FIRE.    THE ELECTRICAL FIRE ON MARCH 9 APPEARS TO HAVE OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF A FAILED SYSTEM WHICH WAS NOT SHUT DOWN BY THE CREW PER THE AFM EMERGENCY CHECKLIST PROCEDURES AFTER A FAILURE WARNING LIGHT ILLUMINATED IN-FLIGHT THE NIGHT BEFORE THE FIRE.  ATTEMPTING TO DISPATCH THE AIRCRAFT THE NEXT DAY WITH INOPERATIVE H STAB DEICE SYSTEM CREATED CONDITIONS LEADING TO MOSFET FIRE IN AFT FUSELAGE DUE TO KNOWN DEFECTS IN THE MOSFET UNITS OF THIS PART NUMBER SERIES.

THE CRASH SITE WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 525 FEET LEFT OF THE RUNWAY 5 CENTERLINE AND APPROXIMATELY 390 FEET SHORT OF THE END OF THE RUNWAY.  SUBSEQUENT TO THE ACCIDENT ON APRIL 15, 2017, IT IS REPORTED THAT MANY AIRCRAFT DEPARTED FROM THE SAME RUNWAY. NONE OF THOSE AIRCRAFT REPORTED SEEING A CRASHED AIRCRAFT OR HEARING AN ELT BEACON TRANSMISSION ON 121.5MHZ. THERE WAS NO FIRE AT THE CRASH SITE, SO THERE WAS NO SMOKE RISING FROM NEAR THE END OF THE RUNWAY THAT WOULD HAVE ALERTED THE PILOTS.  THE FIRST PERSON REPORTED TO SEE THE CRASH SITE WAS AN UNIDENTIFIED PILOT WHO ASKED THE OWNER OF A RESTAURANT ON THE FIELD ABOUT IT EARLY IN THE MORNING ON APRIL 16, 2017. THE RESTAURANT OWNER STATED HE DOES NOT KNOW OR CAN?T REMEMBER THE PILOTS NAME, SO THE PILOT CAN NOT BE LOCATED TO INTERVIEW. THE RESTAURANT OWNER WENT TO SEE THE CRASH SITE AND TOOK A PICTURE OF IT FROM HIS VEHICLE ON THE TAXIWAY AT 0815 WITHOUT CHECKING ANY CLOSER. RESTAURANT OWNER STATES THAT HE DID NOT THINK IT NECESSARY TO CALL 911 OR ALERT ANYONE ELSE TO THE CRASH BECAUSE HE THOUGHT THAT, SINCE IT WAS ON THE AIRFIELD, EVERYONE WOULD ALREADY KNOW.  AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 ON APRIL 16, 2017, THE AIRPORT MANAGER AND HIS WIFE ARRIVED AT THE FIELD TO LAUNCH ANOTHER AIRCRAFT. THE OPERATOR OF THAT AIRCRAFT REPORTED TO THE AIRFIELD MANAGER THAT HE WAS HEARING AN ELT BEACON ON 121.5MHZ. THE AIRFIELD MANAGER MADE A QUICK SWEEP OF THE AIRFIELD RAMP AREA AND THEN WENT TO THE RESTAURANT TO SEE IF ANY PILOTS WERE EATING WHO MAY HAVE KNOWLEDGE ON AN ELT TRANSMITTING. THE RESTAURANT OWNER THEN ASKED THE AIRPORT MANAGER IF HE KNEW ABOUT THE CRASHED AIRCRAFT AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY. THE AIRFIELD MANAGER THEN DROVE WITH HIS WIFE TO THE DEPARTURE END OF RUNWAY 5 AND SAW THE CRASH SITE. HE APPROACHED THE AIRCRAFT CLOSE ENOUGH TO SEE THAT THERE WAS BODIES INSIDE, AND THEN IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED WILLISTON 911 AT 1308. HE THEN ALSO CALLED THE JACKSONVILLE TRACON AND NOTIFIED THEM OF THE CRASH ONCE WILLISTON FIRST RESPONDERS CONFIRMED THE FATALITIES. THE AIRFIELD MANAGER THEN CALLED THE FAA ROCC. HE THEN QUARANTINED HIS FUEL FACILITY AND CALLED SHELL AVIATION TO HAVE IT TESTED.  NOTE: FACTORS WILL BE DETERMINED AT A LATER DATE

I ADVANCED THE THROTTLE SLOWLY BACK TO FULL POWER AND THE ENGINE DID NOT RESPOND.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ NOTICED THIS IMMEDIATELY AND TOOK CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT.  HE CYCLED THE THROTTLE AND STILL NO POWER.  THE ENGINE APPEARED TO REMAIN AT IDLE.  HE CYCLED THE CARBURETOR HEAT AND HAD ME VERIFY THAT WE HAD THE FUEL PUMP ON (WHICH IT WAS.)  NEXT, HE TOLD ME TO TRY TO CRANK THE ENGINE.  I TURNED THE KEY AND NOTHING CHANGED.  BASED ON OUR SINK RATE, THIS WAS ABOUT ALL THE TIME WE HAD TO TROUBLESHOOT BEFORE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ SAID WE WOULD HAVE TO SET THE AIRCRAFT DOWN.  WE WERE UNABLE TO REACH THE FIELD AND IT WAS CLEAR WE WERE HEADED FOR A GROVE OF TREES. CFI STATEMENT:  AFTER ABOUT A HALF HOUR OF PERFORMING SOME AIR WORK AND SIMULATED INSTRUMENT TRAINING MANEUVERS, WE TURNED ON FUEL BOOST PUMP AND THE STUDENT SWITCHED FUEL TANKS. THE STUDENT GLANCED AT THE FUEL IN THE LEFT TANK AND IT WAS REGISTERING JUST ABOVE HALF. THE RIGHT TANK SHOWED SLIGHTLY HIGHER. I LOOKED AND VISUALLY CHECKED THE FUEL SELECTOR AGAINST THE RIGHT DETENT ON THE FUEL SELECTOR. I TOLD HIM TO LEAVE THE FUEL BOOST PUMP ON SINCE OR NEXT MANEUVER WOULD BE THE SIMULATED FORCED LANDING. AFTER FLYING AROUND FOR SEVERAL MINUTES WHILE THE STUDENT GOT HIS BEARINGS, WE DISCUSSED THE PROCEDURES FOR THE SIMULATED FORCED LANDING. THE STUDENT THEN TURNED ON THE CARB HEAT, RETARDED THE THROTTLE TO IDLE AND ESTABLISHED A BEST GLIDE SPEED OF 78 KNOTS. WE STARTED OUR DESCENT FROM 3000 FEET. WE FIRST SELECTED ONE NOTCH OF FLAPS, AND THEN A SECOND NOTCH. I TOLD HIM TO NOTE THAT THE BEECH HAD A SINK RATE OF ABOUT 800 FPM- HIGHER THAN A 150 OR 172. AT 2000 FEET I TOLD THE STUDENT TO SIMULATE UNLATCHING HIS DOOR, AND TOLD HIM THAT WITH THIS SINK RATE WE PROBABLY WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO GLIDE TO THE FIELD AS INTENDED AND TO INITIATE A GO- AROUND. THE STUDENT THEN ADVANCED THE THROTTLE TO THE FORWARD POSITION AND DESELECTED CARB HEAT. THERE WAS NO RESPONSE FROM THE ENGINE. I THEN GRABBED THE THROTTLE AND CYCLED IT BACK AND THEN TO FULL FORWARD AND RESELECTED CARB HEAT. I TOLD THE STUDENT TO CHECK THE MAGS AND TURN THE IGNITION TO START. THAT HAD NO EFFECT. AT THAT TIME THE STUDENT ALSO NOTED THAT WE STILL HAD FUEL PRESSURE. THE LEFT MAIN DID NOT CONTACT THE GROUND UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT WAS ALREADY COMPLETELY OFF THE RUNWAY.  THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH INTERVIEWS STATING THAT THE LEFT MAIN TIRE WAS IN THE AIR WITH THE PILOT INPUT OF FULL RIGHT AILERON EARLY IN THE LANDING ROLL.     THE RESULT OF FULL RIGHT AILERON COMBINED WITH GUSTY WINDS, A TEN DEGREE WING FLAP DEFLECTION ON TOUCHDOWN AND THE INADEQUATE USE OF BACK PRESSURE ON THE YOKE CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT WEIGHT TO SHIFT FORWARD ONTO THE NOSE WHEEL THUS RESULTING IN FORCES SIMILAR TO THOSE ENCOUNTERED WITH A GROUND LOOP. ON THIS OBSERVATION PASS, I SAW CLEAR TRACKS, LIKELY FROM AIRCRAFT WHICH HAD LANDED THERE THE DAY BEFORE. I WAS ALSO ABLE TO CLEARLY SEE THE SLEDS WHICH ARE USED AS AIRSTRIP MARKERS. I THEN REVERSED DIRECTION TO GO DOWN GLACIER, ON A DOWNWIND LEG FOR LANDING, AND CONFIRMED MY INITIAL OBSERVATIONS. BASED UPON THESE OBSERVATIONS AND THE REPORT OF A PILOT WHO HAD LANDED THERE THE DAY BEFORE, I DECIDED TO LAND. I EXECUTED A NORMAL APPROACH AND TOUCHDOWN. THE SNOW ON THE SURFACE WAS DEEPER AND SOFTER THAN I HAD EXPECTED, SO I DECIDED TO NOT STOP AND RISK GETTING STUCK. I SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED A TURNAROUND AT THE TOP OF THE STRIP, BUT WAS UNABLE TO STRAIGHTEN OUT FOR THE TAKE-OFF RUN, AS THE AIRPLANE CONTINUED TO TURN LEFT. MY TAIL SKI WAS LIKELY STUCK IN THE TRACK OF THE RIGHT MAIN SKI. I DECIDED TO KEEP MOVING AND COMPLETE A 360 DEGREE TURN TO GET LINED UP FOR TAKEOFF, WHICH I DID SUCCESSFULLY. ACCELERATION ON THE TAKEOFF RUN WAS INSUFFICIENT TO ACHIEVE FLYING SPEED. THE ATTEMPTED TAKEOFF RUN EXTENDED SOME DISTANCE PAST THE MARKER SLEDS AND THE PREVIOUS TRACKS; PERHAPS 1000 FEET, THOUGH THAT IS JUST A ROUGH ESTIMATE. AT THAT POINT, I DECIDED TO UNDEFINED, BUT IT BECAME MISTY PERHAPS A FEW THOUSAND FEET ABOVE THE LANDING SITE. VISIBILITY BELOW THIS MIST WAS SEVERAL MILES (I COULD CLEARLY SEE UP GLACIER TO THE MOUNTAINS AT THE BACK OF THE RUTH AMPHITHEATER, AND DOWN-GLACIER TO THE MOUNTAINS ON THE EAST MARGIN OF THE GLACIER WHERE IT DISAPPEARS AROUND THE CURVE TO THE SOUTH. THERE WAS NO PRECIPITATION AND THE WIND WAS APPROXIMATELY THREE KNOTS. THE LIGHT WAS VERY FLAT, WHICH I BELIEVE CONTRIBUTED TO MY UNDERESTIMATION OF MY FORWARD SPEED WHEN INITIATING THE TURN. ABORT THE TAKEOFF, AS I WASN'T ACCELERATING ANY FURTHER, AND THE AIRSPEED WAS BELOW THE THRESHOLD OF THE AIRSPEED INDICATOR. MY INTENT WAS TO NOT STOP, BUT TO TURN BACK UPHILL TO RETURN TO THE TOP OF THE STRIP. I RETARDED THE THROTTLE, AND ALLOWED THE AIRCRAFT TO SLOW TO WHAT FELT TO BE A REASONABLE SPEED TO TURN. SHORTLY AFTER INITIATING A LEFT TURN, I FELT THE RIGHT SKI BEGIN TO DIG IN. SHORTLY THEREAFTER, THE AIRCRAFT TURNED INVERTED AND CAME TO REST. AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, THE WEATHER WAS OVERCAST.

I FOUND THAT THE VENTS ON THE BOTTOM OF THE AIRCRAFT WERE PLUGGED WITH TWIGS.  DURING MY INVESTIGATION I FOUND THE MAIN PUMPS WERE STILL IN THE OPEN POSITION WITH GUARDS ON AND THE FUEL TRANSFER PUMPS IN OFF POSITION.  I FLIPPED OFF THE MAIN FUEL PUMPS AFTER TAKING SEVERAL PICTURES WITH AIR METHODS EMPLOYEE AS A WITNESS.  I TOOK SEVERAL MORE PICTURES OF EVERY CONTROL, SWITCHES AND PANEL GAUGES.  I CLIMBED OUT OF THE COCKPIT AND TOOK SOME PICTURES OF THE SKID MARKS AND THE AREA THAT THE HELICOPTER FIRST HIT. AFTER LOOKING AT ALL THE POSSIBILITIES AND TALKING TO EVERYONE INVOLVED WITH THIS OPERATION AND THE AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURER?S  REPRESENTATIVE, IT LOOKS LIKE THE PILOT HAD NOT TURNED THE FUEL TRANSFER PUMPS ON AS REQUIRED BY THE CHECKLIST. THESE PUMPS FEED THE INDIVIDUAL TANKS WHICH FEEDS THE FUEL TO THE ENGINE. IT IS CONCLUDED THAT THE HELICOPTER HAD A DUEL FLAME OUT DUE TO THE FACT THE PILOT DID NOT TURN THE FUEL TRANSFER PUMPS ON.  THIS IS CLEARLY MARKED REQUIRED ITEM THAT IS ON THE CHECK LIST.   THIS INVESTIGATION IS CLOSED FROM FAA SIDE BUT THIS IS STILL BEING INVESTIGATED BY NTSB.  THEY ARE GOING TO DO AN ENGINE TEAR DOWN AND RULE OUT ANY OTHER CAUSES OF ENGINE FAILURES. WEATHER CONDITIONS: TEMP 86 DEG F, DEW POINT 68 DEG F, HUM 55%, WIND NW AT 4.6 MPH, CLEAR 09/07/2017  WE EXAMINED THE ENGINE FROM N561TU TODAY AND FOUND EVIDENCE OF OIL STARVATION, A HOLE IN THE N0.1 PISTON HEAD, A DAMAGED VALVE, AND ENGINE SEIZURE. BASED UPON CALCULATIONS OF FUEL PURCHASES AND FLIGHT TIMES OF 18 DAYS LEADING UP TO THE CRASH INDICATE THAT IT WAS POSSIBLE FOR THE RIGHT WING TO HAVE HAD MINIMAL FUEL. RECORDS OF THE FUELING STATION INDICATE THAT IT WAS PROPERLY MAINTAINED.  FURTHER INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT, ACCOMPLISHED AFTER THE AIRCRAFT REMOVAL FROM THE SCENE, REVEALED THAT THE FUEL SELECTOR VALVE HAD A SHEARED STOP PIN AND WOULD ALLOW THE VALVE TO TRAVEL PAST THE LEFT TANK DETENT. TRAVEL TO THE RIGHT THE STOP PIN WOULD PREVENT TRAVEL PAST THE DETENT. ALTHOUGH, BY MOVING THE SELECTOR PAST THE DETENT WOULD RESULT IN FUEL STARVATION, ALL INDICATIONS FOUND AT THE SCENE WERE THAT THE SELECTOR WAS IN THE LEFT DETENT, WITH NO FACTUAL EVIDENCE THAT IT HAD BEEN MOVED PAST THE DETENT.  TEARDOWN OF THE ENGINE FOUND THE # 3 CYLINDER, EXHAUST VALVE TO BE STUCK IN THE OPEN POSITION. THIS CONDITION WOULD CAUSE THE ENGINE TO RUN ROUGH AND WOULD CAUSE SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF POWER.

POST INCIDENT THE PILOT WAS INTERVIEWED AND STATED THAT HE UNLATCHED/OPENED THE AIRCRAFT CANOPY SLIGHTLY WHILE TAXIING TO THE DEPARTURE RUNWAY AS THE AIRCRAFT COCKPIT WAS GETTING HOT.  HE WENT ON TO STATE THAT HE WAS SURE THAT HE SECURED THE CANOPY PRIOR TO DEPARTURE. ADDITIONALLY HE STATED THAT SOMETIMES WHILE CLOSING/LATCHING THE CANOPY OF THESE AIRCRAFT THAT THEY ARE SOMETIMES STIFF AND REQUIRE ADDITIONAL OR EXTRA AFT MOTION TO ENSURE THEY ARE LATCHED CLOSED. LASTLY HE STATED THAT THIS WAS THE SECOND TIME THAT THIS HAS HAPPENED TO HIM AND THAT THE FIRST TIME HE FAILED TO SECURELY LATCH THE CANOPY. THIS INCIDENT WAS A RESULT OF THE PILOT FAILING TO SECURE THE AIRCRAFT CANOPY.
20170823010659A	A BANNER TOWING SYSTEM IS COMPRISED OF A TOW HITCH WHICH IS MOUNTED AT THE TAIL OF THE AIRCRAFT, CABLE ASSEMBLY, AND RELEASE HANDLE LOCATED IN THE COCKPIT. THE TOW HITCH IS COMPRISED OF AN "OVER CENTER" ARM THAT SECURES THE BANNER TOW ROPE RING. THE TOW RING AND THE ARM ARE HELD IN PLACE WITH A TEMPORARY LOCKING MECHANISM (CLOSE RING) THAT IS CONTROLLED BY THE RELEASE HANDLE IN THE COCKPIT.    THE BANNER TOW LINE IS COMPRISED OF A MOUNTING RING THAT IS SECURED INTO THE TOW HITCH, A LENGTH OF ROPE, A SAFETY LINK THAT IS DESIGNED TO RELEASE THE BANNER WHEN THE DESIGN LOAD IS EXCEEDED, AND A TOW HOOK WITH THREE BARBS SPACED 120 DEGREES APART.    A BANNER IS COMPRISED OF THE LETTERING, LEAD POLE, AND TOW ROPE (MAY ALSO HAVE A SAFETY LINK INSTALLED) WHICH HAS A VERY LARGE LOOP WHICH IS SUSPENDED BETWEEN TOW POLES. THE GIANT LOOP BETWEEN THE POLES IS THE TARGET FOR THE PILOT TO FLY TO AND HAVE THE TOW HOOK SNAG THE LOOP INTO ONE OF THE BARBS.    TO PICK UP A BANNER THE PILOT SECURES THE TOW ROPE INTO THE TOW HITCH AND ROUTES THE TOW ROPE INTO THE COCKPIT AREA. ONCE AIRBORNE THE PILOT RELEASES THE TOW LINE OUT OF THE COCKPIT AND IT BECOMES IN TRAIL WITH THE AIRPLANE. THE PILOT THEN FLIES TO THE BANNER LOOP AND "HOOKS" IT WITH THE TOW HOOK. ONCE HOOKED THE BANNER PEELS OFF OF THE GROUND BACKWARDS AND THEN BECOMES VERTICAL WHEN IN TRAIL DUE TO THE WAY THE LEAD POLE IS MOUNTED TO THE BANNER.   TO DROP A BANNER THE PILOT FLIES OVER THE DROP AREA, PULLS THE RELEASE HANDLE WHICH THEN PULLS THE HITCH CLOSE RING AWAY FROM THE HITCH ARM AND THE BANNER PULLS OUT OF THE HITCH AND FALLS TO THE GROUND.   THE ACCIDENT AIRCRAFT TOOK OFF, RELEASED THE BANNER TOW LINE WHICH WENT INTO TRAIL, AND THEN MADE A NORMAL APPROACH TO THE BANNER LOOP. WHEN THE TOW LINE AND BANNER TOW ROPE ENGAGED (HOOKED) SOMEHOW THE ROPE AND HOOK "SPRUNG" UN-EXPECTANTLY CAUSING THE TOW ROPE AND BANNER ROPE TO WRAP AROUND THE TOW HITCH. ONCE AIRBORNE WITH THE BANNER THE PILOT ATTEMPTED TO RELEASE THE BANNER BUT THE ROPE(S) WERE SOMEHOW WRAPPED AROUND THE HITCH ASSEMBLY PREVENTING THE PILOT FROM PULLING THE RELEASE HANDLE. AT THIS POINT THE BANNER COULD NOT BE RELEASED AND THE PILOT WAS FORCED TO LAND WITH THE BANNER STILL ATTACHED. LANDING WITH THE BANNER ATTACHED THEN CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO RAPIDLY DECELERATE CAUSING IT TO FLIP ONTO ITS NOSE THEN ONTO IT'S BACK. POST ACCIDENT CHECKS ON THE BANNER RELEASE HANDLE AND CABLE WERE COMPLETED AND PROPER OPERATION CONFIRMED. THERE WERE NO SIGNS OF IMPROPER AIRCRAFT OPERATION WITH THE TAKE OFF OR THE TOW HOOK RELEASE.

IT EXITED THE RUNWAY AND RAN INTO A RUNWAY BOX SIGN.    THE PILOT STATED HE DID FLIGHT PLANNING AND CALCULATED THE WEIGHT AND BALANCE FOR THE AIRCRAFT BEFORE THE FLIGHT.  A COPY OF THE WEIGHT AND BALANCE CALCULATION WAS GIVEN TO THE INSPECTOR DURING THE PILOT INTERVIEW.  THE PILOT?S CALCULATION SHOWED THE AIRCRAFT WAS UNDER THE AIRCRAFT?S MAXIMUM TAKEOFF WEIGHT, HOWEVER HE USED AN INCORRECT AIRCRAFT BASIC EMPTY WEIGHT (BEW). USING THE CORRECT BEW PUT THE AIRCRAFT 60 POUNDS OVER THE MAXIMUM CERTIFIED TAKEOFF WEIGHT.  THE PILOT STATED THIS WAS HIS FIRST FLIGHT IN THE CHEROKEE WITH THREE PASSENGERS SINCE HIS AIRCRAFT CHECKOUT.  HIS FIRST FLIGHT IN THE PA-28-161 WAS A 3-HOUR CHECKOUT FLIGHT WITH A FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR ON AUGUST 16, 2017.  THE PILOT?S LOG BOOK ENTRY SHOWS "POWER ON AND POWER OFF, STEEP TURNS, PATTERN AND A CROSS COUNTRY TO KBMI" AND IS SIGNED BY THE CFI.  TWO HOURS AND TWO TENTHS OF THE TOTAL FLIGHT TIME WAS CROSS COUNTRY TIME.  THERE WAS NOT A LOGBOOK ENTRY OF THE NUMBER OR TYPES OF LANDINGS AND TAKEOFFS PERFORMED. THE PILOT?S LOGBOOK DID NOT HAVE ANY ENTRY SHOWING GROUND INSTRUCTION GIVEN BY THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR WITH THE AUGUST 16, 2017 CHEROKEE PA-28-161 CHECKOUT.  THE 457-FOOT SKID PATTERN OF THE LEFT TIRE STARTED APPROXIMATELY 1800 FEET FROM THE END OF RUNWAY 5 AND THE 241-FOOT SKID PATTERN OF THE RIGHT TIRE STARTED APPROXIMATELY 2016 FEET FROM THE END OF RUNWAY 5.  BOTH SKID PATTERNS CONTINUED OFF THE RUNWAY AND INTO THE GRASS.  THE AIRCRAFT WENT OFF THE SIDE OF RUNWAY 5 JUST BEFORE TAXI WAY B3 AND COLLIDED WITH A RUNWAY LIGHT BOX, PUNCTURING THE BOTTOM OF THE LEFT WING FUEL TANK.  THE USABLE LENGTH OF RUNWAY 5 IS 4225 FEET.  EXAMINATION OF THE AIRCRAFT?S TIRES SHOWED ALL THREE TIRES WERE INFLATED, BOTH MAIN TIRES HAD EVEN TREAD WEAR AND THERE WERE NO FLAT SPOTS.  THE RIGHT FUEL TANK LEVEL WAS BELOW THE 17-GALLON FUEL TAB AND THE LEFT TANK WAS ALMOST EMPTY.   INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT'S BRAKES SHOWED THAT BOTH WHEEL BRAKES OPERATED NORMALLY USING THE TOE BRAKES AND THE PARKING BRAKE.  DUE TO THE MINIMAL DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT AND NO SERIOUS INJURIES, THIS WAS CLASSIFIED AS AN ACCIDENT.  COMPLIANCE PHILOSOPHY ACTION

THE PILOT THEN CONTACTED TINIAN FLIGHT SERVICE STATION AND REQUESTED COMPANY MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL BE NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE PROBLEM WITH THE LANDING GEAR AND THAT HE WOULD BE MAKING LOW PASSES OVER THE TINIAN AIRPORT SO THAT A VISUAL ASSESSMENT COULD BE MADE FROM THE GROUND.  AT APPROXIMATELY 17:15 CHST COMPANY MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL ON THE GROUND ON TINIAN WERE ABLE TO VISUALLY VERIFY THAT THE NOSE LANDING GEAR AND LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR APPEARED TO BE FULLY RETRACTED, BUT THE RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR AND BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT MAIN INBOARD GEAR DOORS WERE EXTENDED.  SEVERAL ATTEMPTS WERE MADE TO RE-CYCLE THE LANDING GEAR UP AND DOWN AND THE EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR EXTENSION CHECKLIST WHICH UTILIZES A HAND PUMP SYSTEM WAS PERFORMED WITH NO CHANGE TO THE OBSERVABLE CONFIGURATION OF THE GEAR OR GEAR DOORS.  THE PILOT REPORTED LITTLE TO NO RESISTANCE IN THE HAND PUMP.  MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL ALSO REQUESTED THAT THE PILOT ATTEMPT TO CYCLE THE AIRCRAFT'S ELECTRICAL SYSTEM OFF AND BACK ON AND TO DE-ACTIVATE THE LANDING GEAR SAFETY CIRCUIT BREAKER TO SEE IF ANY OBSERVABLE CHANGE WOULD TAKE PLACE.  NO CHANGE TO THE LANDING GEAR POSITION WAS SEEN AND NO CHANGE TO THE AIRCRAFT'S GEAR INDICATION WAS OBSERVED.  AT 18:06 CHST THE AIRCRAFT WAS CLEARED TO LAND ON TEMPORARY RUNWAY 24.   AT 18:08 CHST THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON RUNWAY 24.  DURING THE LANDING THE RIGHT GEAR RETRACTED AND THE LEFT WING TIP CONTACTED THE GROUND CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO VEER TO THE LEFT OFF THE RUNWAY AND ONTO THE GRASS BETWEEN RUNWAYS 24 AND 25 APPROXIMATELY 75 FEET WEST OF TAXIWAY DELTA.  THE FIVE PASSENGERS ON BOARD EXITED THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE RIGHT EMERGENCY EXIT AND THE PILOT AND NON-PILOT CREWMEMBER EXITED VIA THE AIRCRAFT'S LEFT FORWARD CREW DOOR. NO OTHER PROPERTY DAMAGE WAS NOTED AND NO PERSONS WERE HARMED ON THE GROUND.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS REMOVED FROM THE ACCIDENT SCENE AND RELOCATED TO GREELY, COLORADO FOR A TEAR-DOWN INSPECTION. IN 2014, AIRBUS HELICOPTERS PUBLISHED A SAFETY NOTICE (NO. 2630-S-29) STATING THAT RECENT ACCIDENTS AND INCIDENTS WHICH OCCURRED DURING HYDRAULIC FAILURE TRAINING LED THEM TO RELEASE THE NOTICE AS A REMINDER TO COMPLY WITH THE "CAUTION" IN THE FLIGHT MANUAL EMERGENCY PROCEDURES.   THE CAUTION REQUIRES THAT NO HOVER FLIGHT OR MANEUVERS AT LOW SPEED BE PERFORMED IN THE CONFIGURATION REQUIRED FOR THE HYDRAULIC FAILURE TRAINING. IN THAT FLIGHT CONFIGURATION, THE INTENSITY AND DIRECTION OF THE LOAD RETURN FROM THE MAIN ROTOR THROUGH THE CONTROLS "MAY RAPIDLY CHANGE AND GENERATE A SIGNIFICANT WORKLOAD FOR THE PILOT, THUS CAUSING A RISK OF LOSS OF CONTROL OF THE HELICOPTER".  IT IS OF MY OPINION THAT DURING EXECUTION OF THE HYDRAULIC FAILURE TRAINING, THE CREW OF THE AS-350B2 MANEUVERED AT AN AIRSPEED WHICH WAS TOO LOW AND CAUSED LOSS OF CONTROL AS DESCRIBED BY THE AIRBUS SAFETY INFORMATION NOTICE.

TOXICOLOGY SAMPLES WERE TAKEN BY THE LUBBOCK MEDICAL EXAMINER AND SENT TO CAMI AND THE FINAL TOXICOLOGY REPORT HAS BEEN RECEIVED FROM CAMI.  THE AMT TRAINING RECORDS SHOWED THAT THE MECHANIC WAS TRAINED AND QUALIFIED FOR THE TASK HE WAS PERFORMING. HE WAS WORKING A NORMAL SHIFT WITH ADEQUATE DAYS AND HOURS OFF FOR THE PRECEDING 30-DAY PERIOD.  LUBBOCK FSDO PERSONNEL HAVE DETERMINED THAT A SINGLE NOSE LANDING GEAR DOOR ACTUATOR SAFETY LOCK, PART # C47281, IS AVAILABLE ON STATION. INTERVIEWS WITH FEDEX PERSONNEL CONFIRM THAT NEITHER THE RIGHT HAND NOR THE LEFT HAND NOSE LANDING GEAR DOORS HAD ACTUATOR LOCKS INSTALLED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT. THE LEFT NOSE GEAR DOOR GROUND OPENING CONTROL HANDLE WAS DISCOVERED IN THE OPEN POSITION. FOR THIS REASON THE DOOR STAYED OPEN WHILE HYDRAULICS WAS ON. THE RIGHT NOSE GEAR DOOR GROUND OPENING CONTROL HANDLE WAS IN THE CLOSED POSITION. AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE MANUAL STANDARD PRACTICES CONCERNING THE NOSE LANDING GEAR HAS A WARNING MESSAGE THAT STATES, ?WHEN DOORS ARE OPEN, MAKE CERTAIN THAT SAFETY COLLARS ARE POSITIONED ON DOOR ACTUATING CYLINDERS.?

HE THEN CALLED THE ASOS AT ORANGE MUNICIPAL AIRPORT (ORE) TO GET WEATHER CONDITIONS. HE STATES THEY WERE 10 PLUS VISIBILITY, CLEAR SKY, AND LITTLE WIND. THE OBSERVATION WAS VERIFIED BY INSPECTOR IN CHARGE (IIC) FOR 2:52 PM AND SHOWED 17005KT FOR WINDS. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATED THE HE DID NOT RECEIVE A FORMAL WEATHER BRIEF. THE INTENDED FLIGHT WAS TO ORE. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STARTED THE AIRCRAFT AND COMPLETED HIS PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATED THAT ALL WAS WELL WITH THE AIRPLANE AND THE BRAKES WERE WORKING FINE AS HE TAXIED IT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ THEN TOOK THE ACTIVE RUNWAY 16 AND VERIFIED RUDDER PEDAL OPERATION.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ STATED THAT HE THEN APPLIED FULL THROTTLE AND ATTEMPTED TAKE-OFF. HE STATED THAT AT ABOUT 200 FEET AND 50 KNOTS HE LOST CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT WHILE HOLDING THE CONTROLS IN A TAIL UP POSITION. THE AIRCRAFT MADE A HARD LEFT TURN. THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED THE RUNWAY UNDER POWER AT APPROXIMATELY 400 FEET FROM THE END OF RUNWAY 16. THE AIRCRAFT THEN WENT DOWN AND BACK UP A SMALL DITCH THAT RUNS PARALLEL TO THE RUNWAY. WHEN THE AIRCRAFT WENT BACK UP THE DITCH, THE RIGHT LANDING GEAR BROKE AND THE AIRCRAFT TEMPORARILY BECAME AIRBORNE. THE AIRCRAFT STARTED TO ROLL OVER AND ITS LEFT LOWER WING AND PROPELLER IMPACTED THE GROUND WHILE UNDER POWER. THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO ITS FINAL RESTING PLACE APPROXIMATELY 150 FEET PAST WHERE IT EXITED THE RUNWAY AND 175 FEET THE LEFT EDGE OF RUNWAY 16. THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO REST UPSIDE DOWN AND FACING THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION OF ITS INTENDED DEPARTURE. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ WAS ABLE TO CRAWL OUT OF THE AIRCRAFT. HE HAS STATED THAT HE RECEIVED NO INJURIES OTHER THAN MINOR BRUISING.  THE IIC FOUND THERE TO BE SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. BOTH PROPELLER BLADE TIPS WERE BENT BACK APPROXIMATELY 90 DEGREES COUPLED WITH THE GROUND SCORING FOUND INDICATES THAT THE ENGINE WAS UNDER POWER WHEN THE PROPELLER CAME INTO CONTACT WITH THE GROUND. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ (MECHANIC AT THE AIRFIELD) STATED THAT WHEN HE WENT TO THE AIRCRAFT RIGHT AFTER THE ACCIDENT, THEN HE CRAWLED INTO THE PLANE, SHUT THE FUEL SELECTOR, PULLED THE THROTTLE BACK TO IDLE POSITION FROM ITS FULL POWER POSITION AS WELL AS RETURN MIXTURE TO IDLE CUTOFF MAKING SURE NO OTHER FUEL COULD FLOW TO THE ENGINE. ALL THREE WHEELS ROTATED FREELY AND NO FLAT SPOTS WERE NOTED ON THE TIRES. THE RIGHT BRAKE ASSEMBLY BROKE OFF AND APPEARED TO HAPPEN AS A RESULT OF THE ACCIDENT AND NOT CONTRIBUTING TO IT. DARK TIRE MARKS WERE MADE BY THE RIGHT WHEEL ON THE RUNWAY INDICATING THAT THE AIRCRAFT?S WEIGHT WAS HEAVY ON THE RIGHT WHEEL. THE MARKS FROM THE LEFT WHEEL WERE TOO LIGHT TO CAPTURE BY CAMERA INDICATING THE AIRCRAFT WAS VERY LIGHT ON THE LEFT TIRE. THERE WERE SQUIGGLY TIRE MARKS ON THE RUNWAY FROM THE TAIL WHEEL INDICATING THAT THE TAIL WHEEL WAS ON THE GROUND DURING ITS LEFT TURN. FLIGHT CONTROL FUNCTION WAS VERIFIED BY THE IIC AND SHOW NO EVIDENCE OF A MALFUNCTION.

BOTH PROPELLER BLADES WERE SLIGHTLY BENT FROM IMPACT AND UPPER AND LOWER COWLINGS WERE DAMAGED. THE RIGHT SIDE FIREWALL WAS WRINKLED AND THE RIGHT LOWER ENGINE MOUNT WAS BENT. THE RIGHT WING TOP SKIN WAS WRINKLED AND BUCKLED AND THE LEADING EDGE WAS TORN OPEN JUST OUTBOARD OF THE FUEL TANK. THE LEFT WING TOP SKIN TWO FEET FROM THE WING TIP WAS WRINKLED AND THE FIBERGLASS WING TIP WAS TORN OPEN. THE RIGHT WINDSHIELD WAS BROKEN AND DISLODGED AND THE FUSELAGE WAS BUCKLED JUST ABOVE THE LEFT WING ROOT. THE FLAPS WERE IN THE FULL UP POSITION. THE THROTTLE WAS FULLY RETARDED AND THE MIXTURE WAS FULL RICH. THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS ON THE LEFT TANK.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS BROUGHT TO A LEVEL ATTITUDE AND BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT WING FUEL CAPS WERE REMOVED AND NO FUEL WAS NOTED IN EITHER TANK. PERSONNEL WHO WERE REMOVING BOTH WINGS DURING THE SALVAGE OPERATION STATED THAT APPROXIMATELY ONE HALF GALLON OF FUEL WAS REMOVED FROM BOTH WINGS.  THE PILOT STATED THE FOLLOWING: PRIOR TO LEAVING OXFORD AIRPORT HE VISUALLY CHECKED BOTH TANKS AND CONFIRMED THAT THE FUEL LEVELS WERE AT THE TABS. THIS WOULD GIVE HIM 18 GALLONS PER SIDE REMAINING FOR A TOTAL OF 36 GALLONS. HE USED AOPA FLIGHT PLANER TO CALCULATE THE 218 MILE TRIP WITH A FUEL BURN OF 8 GALLONS PER HOUR, AN AIR SPEED OF 103 KNOTS, AND A HEAD WIND OF 37 KNOTS. THESE CALCULATION RESULTS WOULD REQUIRE 28 GALLONS OF FUEL WITH A GROUND SPEED OF 69 MPH FOR A TOTAL FLIGHT TIME OF 3:09 HOURS LEAVING THEM 6 GALLONS OF RESERVE. HE TOOK OFF FROM 81B AT APPROXIMATELY 13:30 AND CLIMB TO AN ALTITUDE 4500?. HE ELECTED TO USE ALL THE FUEL IN THE RIGHT TANK FIRST WHICH RAN DRY JUST PAST WORCESTER APPROXIMATELY 150 MILES INTO THE TRIP WHERE HE SWITCHED TO THE LEFT TANK FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE TRIP. HE DESCENDED ALTITUDE SEVERAL TIMES LOOKING FOR LESS HEADWIND BUT MAINTAINED A GROUND SPEED OF 68-73 KNOTS THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE TRIP. JUST NORTH EAST OF HARTFORD BRAINARD (HFD) HE NOTICED THE LEFT FUEL QUANTITY NEEDLE BOUNCING BELOW THE 10 GALLON MARK, BUT WAS CONFIDENT IN HIS CALCULATIONS AND ELECTED NOT TO STOP AT HFD FOR FUEL. AT 2.5 MILES OUT FROM MMK THE FUEL PRESSURE GAGE FALTERED AND IT BECAME CLEAR THEY WOULD NOT MAKE THE RUNWAY. THEY SETUP FOR BEST GLIDE SPEED AND PREPARED THE AIRCRAFT FOR AN EMERGENCY LANDING. AT 16:13 THEY IMPACTED THE CHAIN LINK FENCE.

BOMBARDIER SERVICE LETTER DH8-400-SL-24-016 INDICATES THAT THIS IS A KNOWN ISSUE WITH THESE CONNECTORS. THE CONNECTOR CONTAINS 3 8 GAUGE AC POWER WIRES FROM THE LH AC CIRCUIT BREAKER BOX LOCATED IN THE NACELLE. THE "P" CONNECTOR ATTACHED TO THE WIRES OUTSIDE AND INSIDE THE FUSE ARE DAMAGED AND REQUIRE REPLACEMENT. THE CONNECTOR JACK IS ALSO DAMAGED AND REQUIRES REPLACEMENT.   FURTHER INSPECTIONS ARE CURRENTLY UNDERWAY AND THE AIRCRAFT REMAINS ONN THE GROUND UNTIL REPAIRS ARE CARRIED OUT. FURTHER UPDATES WILL BE ADDED TO THIS SDR AS THE INFORMATION BECOMES AVAILABLE.
