WEATHER CONDITIONS AT THE ACCIDENT SCENE WERE INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (IMC).    ON THE INITIAL APPROACH INTO SPI, THE PIC ATTEMPTED THE INSTRUMENT LANDING SYSTEM (ILS) FOR RUNWAY 31.  PRIOR TO THE APPROACH THE PIC NOTIFIED SPI APPROACH CONTROL THAT HE WAS NOT PICKING UP THE NAVIGATION SIGNAL FOR THE ILS 31.  ATC NOTIFIED THE PIC OF THE CORRECT FREQUENCY.  THE PIC HAD INITIALLY TUNED IN AN INCORRECT FREQUENCY.  THE AIRCRAFT PASSED BACK AND FORTH ACROSS THE FINAL APPROACH PATH AND HAD DIFFICULTY REMAINING ESTABLISHED ON THE APPROACH.  SPI APPROACH CONTROL ASKED THE PIC IF THE AIRCRAFT WAS ESTABLISHED ON THE LOCALIZER AND RECEIVING THE GLIDE SLOPE INDICATIONS.  THE PILOT RESPONDED THAT THEY WERE.  SPI APPROACH CONTROL THEN INSTRUCTED N6071R TO CONTACT SPI TOWER CONTROL.  SPI TOWER CONTROL THEN CLEARED N6071R FOR LANDING.  SPI TOWER CONTROL ADVISED THE PIC THAT HE APPEARED TO BE LEFT OF COURSE AND THE PIC REPLIED "CORRECTING".  SPI TOWER CONTROL THEN ADVISED THE PIC THAT THE AIRPLANE APPEARED TO BE ON COURSE.  THE PIC RESPONDED "IT LOOKS LIKE WE WENT THROUGH THE COURSE."  THE AIRCRAFT WAS WELL RIGHT OF COURSE WHEN THE SPI TOWER CONTROLLER INSTRUCTED N6071R TO CANCEL ANY CLEARANCE, CLIMB AND MAINTAIN 3,000 MSL, AND TURN RIGHT TO HEADING 360.  SPI TOWER CONTROL ADVISED N6071R THAT SPI DEPARTURE CONTROL WOULD VECTOR THEM AROUND FOR ANOTHER APPROACH AND THAT THE PRIOR APPROACH "DIDN'T LOOK SAFE FROM HERE".  SPI TOWER CONTROL THEN ADVISED N6071R TO CONTACT DEPARTURE CONTROL.  SPI APPROACH CONTROL ASKED THE PIC IF HE WOULD LIKE VECTORS BACK TO THE ILS 31 APPROACH OR CHANGE TO THE ILS 22 APPROACH.  THE PIC REPLIED HE WOULD LIKE TO GO BACK TO THE ILS 31.  SPI APPROACH CONTROL ASKED THE PIC IF HE WAS HAVING ISSUES WITH HIS "NAV HEAD" AND THE PIC REPLIED "YUP".  SPI APPROACH CONTROL THEN ASKED IF THE PIC WOULD LIKE AN APPROACH SURVEILLANCE RADAR (ASR) APPROACH.  DUE TO SEVERAL SUBSEQUENT INTERMITTENT RADIO TRANSMISSIONS SPI APPROACH CONTROL ASKED THE PIC IF HE WAS HAVING ELECTRICAL ISSUES TO WHICH HE REPLIED "THAT'S NEGATIVE."  AT THIS TIME THE PIC NOTIFIED SPI APPROACH CONTROL THAT THEY WOULD FLY THE ILS 31 APPROACH AGAIN AND THAT THEY WERE "PICKING UP A LITTLE ICE".  SPI APPROACH CONTROL AGAIN OFFERED THE PIC AN ASR APPROACH AND THE PIC RESPONDED "OKAY, NO WE WILL TRY IT AGAIN, IT JUST, AH, TOOK OFF WHEN WE, AH WHEN WE WERE AH ABOUT 2300."  SPI APPROACH CONTROL BEGAN GIVING N6071R VECTORS BACK FOR THE ILS 31 APPROACH AND ASKED IF THEY WERE STILL IN ICING CONDITIONS.  THE PIC RESPONDED THAT THEY WERE ABOVE THE ICING CONDITIONS AT 3,000 FEET MSL.  SPI APPROACH CONTROL THEN ASKED THE PIC IF THE LANDING GEAR WAS STILL EXTENDED.  THE PIC ACKNOWLEDGED THAT THE LANDING GEAR WAS STILL EXTENDED.  ON THE SECOND APPROACH THE AIRCRAFT PASSED THROUGH APPROACH COURSE AND PARALLELED IT INBOUND.  THE AIRCRAFT REMAINED LEFT OF THE APPROACH COURSE NEVER BECOMING ESTABLISHED ON THE INBOUND COURSE. THE MITIGATION/CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TAKEN BY THE AIRMAN INCLUDED ELIMINATING THE COMPLACENT BEHAVIOR OF PERFORMING MAINTENANCE TASK BY MEMORY AND PARTICIPATION IN A COMPANY-WIDE MAINTENANCE SAFETY BRIEFING THAT EMPHASIZED THE IMPORTANCE OF REFERENCING CURRENT MANUFACTURES MAINTENANCE MANUALS AND LOOKING AT THE ?BIG PICTURE? THE HAND CAMERA ON THE TANDEM MASTER WAS A SINGLE VELCRO BAND JUST ABOVE HIS WRIST WHICH COULD HAVE BEEN RELEASED INSTEAD OF UNTANGLING THE CONTROL LINE TO FREE HIMSELF. THE TANDEM MASTER THEN INITIATES A RELEASE OF THE RESERVE PARACHUTE AT OR BELOW 240 FT AGL, OR 75 SECONDS UNDER CANOPY, BY RELEASING THE RSL, RESERVE STATIC LINE. THIS ACTION BEGAN A RESERVE DEPLOYMENT AND PARTIAL SEPARATION OF THE MAIN CANOPY, LEFT RISER, AT THE SAME TIME, AT AN ALTITUDE FAR TO LOW FOR A SUCCESSFUL RESERVE DEPLOYMENT. THIS ACTION ACTUALLY SPED UP THE DESCENT WHERE THE JUMPERS WERE FATALLY INJURED FROM IMPACT AT 78 SECONDS FROM INITIAL DEPLOYMENT OF THE PARACHUTE.

CAUSE: THE STUDENT ATTEMPTED TO STRETCH HIS GLIDE TO ?MAKE HIS SPOT?, FLARED TOO HIGH AND HAD A HARD LANDING. ?	PREVENTION DISCUSSED FOR THE INSTRUCTOR AND STUDENT: PAY MORE ATTENTION TO THE ?FEEL? OF THE AIRCRAFT.  BE AWARE THAT IF ?SINKING? IS FELT, IT IS TIME TO LOWER THE NOSE, ADD POWER, AND PERFORM A GO-AROUND. TODAY WE DISCUSSED THAT PILOTS CANNOT SEE EVERYTHING THAT NEEDS TO BE OBSERVED IN ORDER TO DETERMINE IF AN AIRCRAFT IS SAFE TO FLY AFTER A HARD LANDING. WE DISCUSSED THE FACT THAT BY NOT BEING QUALIFIED TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE, AND NOT SQUAWKING THE AIRCRAFT FOR A HARD LANDING, THE PILOT AND INSTRUCTOR JEOPARDIZED THE SAFETY OF THOSE WHO WERE SCHEDULED TO FLY IN THE AIRCRAFT AFTER THEM.  AFTER CONFERRING WITH AN OPS FLM, FAA IIC HAS DECIDED THAT NO FURTHER ACTION IS NEEDED AND THAT THE COUNSELING PROVIDE BY THE FLIGHT SCHOOL IS AN ADEQUATE CORRECTIVE ACTION FOR THIS TRAINING MISTAKE.

AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, THE AERIAL APPLICATION WAS BEING CONDUCTED 14.5 STATUTE MILES EAST/NORTHEAST FROM MCKELLAR-SIPES REGIONAL AIRPORT/JACKSON, TN (MKL).  THE PIC STATED THAT HE WAS PULLING UP FROM HIS LAST SWATH RUN BEFORE RETURNING TO MKL WHEN THE ENGINE FAILED.  THE PIC ELECTED TO ATTEMPT AN EMERGENCY LANDING ON HIGHWAY 20 EASTBOUND.  AN ON SCENE POST-ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION CONDUCTED BY THE MEMPHIS FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE REVEALED THAT THE LANDING GEAR COLLAPSED UPON TOUCHDOWN.  THE AIRCRAFT VEERED OFF INTO THE RIGHT DITCH WHERE THE RIGHT WING STRUCK A TREE CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO ABRUPTLY YAW TO THE RIGHT.  THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO REST PERPENDICULAR TO THE ROADWAY AND NOSE DOWN INTO THE TREE LINE PARALLEL TO THE ROAD.  THE PILOT WAS UNINJURED.  NO POST-ACCIDENT FIRE OCCURRED AND NO ODOR OF FUEL WAS PRESENT AT THE SITE.  THE APPLICATION PAYLOAD WAS EXHAUSTED.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS MOVED OFF THE ROADWAY TO A SAFER LOCATION ABOUT 100 YARDS TO THE EAST OF THE CRASH SITE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION.  THE RIGHT AND LEFT FUEL TANK APPEARED TO BE INTACT.  REMOVAL OF THE FUEL TANK INSPECTION PANELS SHOWED ZERO FUEL IN EITHER OF THE TANKS.  INSPECTION OF THE MAIN FUEL LINE AT THE FIREWALL REVEALED ONLY A TRACE AMOUNT OF FUEL.  INSPECTION OF THE HIGH PRESSURE FUEL LINE BETWEEN THE HIGH PRESSURE PUMP AND THE FUEL CONTROL UNIT REVEALED ONLY A TRACE AMOUNT OF FUEL. PROBABLE CAUSE OF THE ACCIDENT WAS FOUND TO BE THE PIC?S FAILURE TO MAINTAIN ADEQUATE AIRSPEED RESULTING IN LOSS OF CONTROL DURING AN EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER AN ENGINE FAILURE.  THE MAJOR CONTRIBUTING FACTOR WAS THE ENGINE FAILURE, CAUSED BY FUEL EXHAUSTION.

DURING AN INTERVIEW WITH THE PIC HE STATED THAT IT WAS HIS INTENTION TO PERFORM A QUICK MAINTENANCE FLIGHT TO TROUBLESHOOT A VIBRATION THAT WAS COMING FROM THE INSTRUMENT PANEL.  DUE TO THE CURRENT WIND CONDITIONS THE DECISION WAS MADE TO DEPART RUNWAY 090 AND TO PERFORM TWO TOUCH & GO?S AND A FULL STOP.  BOTH TOUCH AND GO?S WERE UNEVENTFUL AS HE PREPARED FOR HIS FINAL LANDING AND STOP.  AS HE LINED UP TO LAND HE NOTICED THAT THE WIND HAD SHIFTED AND WAS CAUSING HIS SPEED TO INCREASE AS HE TRIED TO COMPENSATE WITH A DECREASE IN THROTTLE.  AT THIS POINT THE AIRCRAFT WAS ALREADY AT THE START OF THE RUNWAY SO THE DECISION WAS MADE TO GO AHEAD AND LAND ON 090.  AS THE AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN THE PIC NOTICED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS STILL ACCELERATING AS HE NOTICED THE WIND HAD SHIFTED AND WAS AT 270 AND NOT 090, CAUSING A TAILWIND EFFECT.  UNFORTUNATELY AT THIS POINT THERE WAS NOT ENOUGH RUNWAY LEFT TO ATTEMPT AN ABORTED LANDING SO THE DECISION WAS MADE TO MAKE EVERY EFFORT TO APPLY EXCESSIVE BREAKING TO STOP THE AIRCRAFT.  HOWEVER, DUE TO THE EXCESSIVE LANDING SPEED THE AIRCRAFT WAS UNABLE TO SLOW DOWN IN A TIMELY MANNER BEFORE RUNNING OUT OF RUNWAY.  FINALLY, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO MAKE A WIDE RIGHT TURN TO HOPEFULLY ASSIST THE AIRCRAFT DECELERATE.  THIS MANEUVER CAUSED THE RIGHT WING TO LIFT IN THE AIR WHICH RESULTED IN THE AIRCRAFT BECOMING INVERTED BEFORE FINALLY COMING TO A COMPLETE STOP. DURING ALL THE COMMOTION THE PIC STRUCK HIS HEAD ON THE INSTRUMENT PANEL AND WAS TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL MEDICAL FACILITY TO BE EVALUATED.
